24998.label: Luke 1:1
24998.text: Seeing that many have undertaken to compile an account of the facts that are given full credence among us,

24999.label: Luke 1:2
24999.text: just as these were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and attendants of the message,

25000.label: Luke 1:3
25000.text: I resolved also, because I have traced all things from the start with accuracy, to write them to you in logical order, most excellent The·ophʹi·lus,

25001.label: Luke 1:4
25001.text: so that you may know fully the certainty of the things that you have been taught orally.

25002.label: Luke 1:5
25002.text: In the days of Herod, king of Ju·deʹa, there was a priest named Zech·a·riʹah of the division of A·biʹjah. His wife was from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.

25003.label: Luke 1:6
25003.text: They both were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in accord with all the commandments and legal requirements of Jehovah.

25004.label: Luke 1:7
25004.text: But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and they both were well along in years.

25005.label: Luke 1:8
25005.text: Now as he was serving as priest in the assignment of his division before God,

25006.label: Luke 1:9
25006.text: according to the established practice of the priesthood it became his turn to offer incense when he entered into the sanctuary of Jehovah.

25007.label: Luke 1:10
25007.text: And the entire multitude of the people were praying outside at the hour of offering incense.

25008.label: Luke 1:11
25008.text: Jehovah’s angel appeared to him, standing at the right side of the incense altar.

25009.label: Luke 1:12
25009.text: But Zech·a·riʹah became troubled at the sight, and he was overcome with fear.

25010.label: Luke 1:13
25010.text: However, the angel said to him: “Do not be afraid, Zech·a·riʹah, because your supplication has been favorably heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to name him John.

25011.label: Luke 1:14
25011.text: You will have joy and great gladness, and many will rejoice over his birth,

25012.label: Luke 1:15
25012.text: for he will be great in the sight of Jehovah. But he must drink no wine or any alcoholic drink at all, and he will be filled with holy spirit even from before birth,

25013.label: Luke 1:16
25013.text: and he will turn back many of the sons of Israel to Jehovah their God.

25014.label: Luke 1:17
25014.text: Also, he will go ahead of him with E·liʹjah’s spirit and power, to turn back the hearts of fathers to children and the disobedient ones to the practical wisdom of righteous ones, in order to get ready for Jehovah a prepared people.”

25015.label: Luke 1:18
25015.text: Zech·a·riʹah said to the angel: “How can I be sure of this? For I am old, and my wife is well along in years.”

25016.label: Luke 1:19
25016.text: In reply the angel said to him: “I am Gaʹbri·el, who stands near before God, and I was sent to speak with you and to declare this good news to you.

25017.label: Luke 1:20
25017.text: But look! you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things take place, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their appointed time.”

25018.label: Luke 1:21
25018.text: Meanwhile, the people continued waiting for Zech·a·riʹah, and they were surprised that he delayed so long in the sanctuary.

25019.label: Luke 1:22
25019.text: When he came out, he was unable to speak to them, and they perceived that he had just seen a supernatural sight in the sanctuary. He kept making signs to them but remained speechless.

25020.label: Luke 1:23
25020.text: When the days of his holy service were completed, he went off to his home.

25021.label: Luke 1:24
25021.text: Some days later Elizabeth his wife became pregnant, and she kept herself secluded for five months, saying:

25022.label: Luke 1:25
25022.text: “This is how Jehovah has dealt with me in these days. He has turned his attention to me to take away my reproach among men.”

25023.label: Luke 1:26
25023.text: In her sixth month, the angel Gaʹbri·el was sent from God to a city of Galʹi·lee named Nazʹa·reth,

25024.label: Luke 1:27
25024.text: to a virgin promised in marriage to a man named Joseph of David’s house, and the name of the virgin was Mary.

25025.label: Luke 1:28
25025.text: And coming in, the angel said to her: “Greetings, you highly favored one, Jehovah is with you.”

25026.label: Luke 1:29
25026.text: But she was deeply disturbed at his words and tried to understand what kind of greeting this might be.

25027.label: Luke 1:30
25027.text: So the angel said to her: “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.

25028.label: Luke 1:31
25028.text: And look! you will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and you are to name him Jesus.

25029.label: Luke 1:32
25029.text: This one will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and Jehovah God will give him the throne of David his father,

25030.label: Luke 1:33
25030.text: and he will rule as King over the house of Jacob forever, and there will be no end to his Kingdom.”

25031.label: Luke 1:34
25031.text: But Mary said to the angel: “How is this to be, since I am not having sexual relations with a man?”

25032.label: Luke 1:35
25032.text: In answer the angel said to her: “Holy spirit will come upon you, and power of the Most High will overshadow you. And for that reason the one who is born will be called holy, God’s Son.

25033.label: Luke 1:36
25033.text: And look! Elizabeth your relative has also conceived a son, in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her, the so-called barren woman;

25034.label: Luke 1:37
25034.text: for no declaration will be impossible for God.”

25035.label: Luke 1:38
25035.text: Then Mary said: “Look! Jehovah’s slave girl! May it happen to me according to your declaration.” At that the angel departed from her.

25036.label: Luke 1:39
25036.text: So Mary set out in those days and traveled with haste into the mountainous country, to a city of Judah,

25037.label: Luke 1:40
25037.text: and she entered the home of Zech·a·riʹah and greeted Elizabeth.

25038.label: Luke 1:41
25038.text: Well, as Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary, the infant in her womb leaped, and Elizabeth was filled with holy spirit

25039.label: Luke 1:42
25039.text: and loudly cried out: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruitage of your womb!

25040.label: Luke 1:43
25040.text: So how is it that this privilege is mine, to have the mother of my Lord come to me?

25041.label: Luke 1:44
25041.text: For look! as the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy.

25042.label: Luke 1:45
25042.text: Happy too is she who believed, for there will be a complete fulfillment of those things spoken to her from Jehovah.”

25043.label: Luke 1:46
25043.text: And Mary said: “My soul magnifies Jehovah,

25044.label: Luke 1:47
25044.text: and my spirit cannot keep from being overjoyed at God my Savior,

25045.label: Luke 1:48
25045.text: because he has looked upon the low position of his slave girl. For look! from now on all generations will declare me happy,

25046.label: Luke 1:49
25046.text: because the powerful One has done great deeds for me, and holy is his name,

25047.label: Luke 1:50
25047.text: and for generation after generation his mercy is upon those who fear him.

25048.label: Luke 1:51
25048.text: He has acted mightily with his arm; he has scattered those who are haughty in the intention of their hearts.

25049.label: Luke 1:52
25049.text: He has brought down powerful men from thrones and has exalted lowly ones;

25050.label: Luke 1:53
25050.text: he has fully satisfied hungry ones with good things and has sent away empty-handed those who had wealth.

25051.label: Luke 1:54
25051.text: He has come to the aid of Israel his servant, remembering his mercy,

25052.label: Luke 1:55
25052.text: just as he spoke to our forefathers, to Abraham and to his offspring, forever.”

25053.label: Luke 1:56
25053.text: Mary stayed with her about three months and then returned to her own home.

25054.label: Luke 1:57
25054.text: The time now came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she gave birth to a son.

25055.label: Luke 1:58
25055.text: And the neighbors and her relatives heard that Jehovah had magnified his mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.

25056.label: Luke 1:59
25056.text: On the eighth day they came to circumcise the young child, and they were going to name him after his father, Zech·a·riʹah.

25057.label: Luke 1:60
25057.text: But his mother said in reply: “No! but he will be called John.”

25058.label: Luke 1:61
25058.text: At this they said to her: “Not one of your relatives is called by this name.”

25059.label: Luke 1:62
25059.text: Then they asked his father by signs what he wanted him to be called.

25060.label: Luke 1:63
25060.text: So he asked for a tablet and wrote: “John is his name.” At this they were all amazed.

25061.label: Luke 1:64
25061.text: Instantly his mouth was opened and his tongue was set free and he began to speak, praising God.

25062.label: Luke 1:65
25062.text: And fear fell upon all those living in their neighborhood, and all these things began to be talked about in the whole mountainous country of Ju·deʹa.

25063.label: Luke 1:66
25063.text: And all who heard noted it in their hearts, saying: “What will this young child turn out to be?” For the hand of Jehovah was indeed with him.

25064.label: Luke 1:67
25064.text: Then Zech·a·riʹah his father was filled with holy spirit, and he prophesied, saying:

25065.label: Luke 1:68
25065.text: “Let Jehovah be praised, the God of Israel, because he has turned his attention to his people and has brought them deliverance.

25066.label: Luke 1:69
25066.text: And he has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his servant,

25067.label: Luke 1:70
25067.text: just as he has spoken through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old,

25068.label: Luke 1:71
25068.text: of a salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all those hating us;

25069.label: Luke 1:72
25069.text: to show mercy in connection with our forefathers and to call to mind his holy covenant,

25070.label: Luke 1:73
25070.text: the oath that he swore to Abraham our forefather,

25071.label: Luke 1:74
25071.text: to grant us, after we have been rescued from the hands of enemies, the privilege of fearlessly rendering sacred service to him

25072.label: Luke 1:75
25072.text: with loyalty and righteousness before him all our days.

25073.label: Luke 1:76
25073.text: But as for you, young child, you will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go ahead of Jehovah to prepare his ways,

25074.label: Luke 1:77
25074.text: to give knowledge of salvation to his people by forgiveness of their sins,

25075.label: Luke 1:78
25075.text: because of the tender compassion of our God. With this compassion a daybreak will visit us from on high,

25076.label: Luke 1:79
25076.text: to give light to those sitting in darkness and death’s shadow and to guide our feet in the way of peace.”

25077.label: Luke 1:80
25077.text: And the young child grew up and became strong in spirit, and he continued in the desert until the day he showed himself openly to Israel.

25078.label: Luke 2:1
25078.text: Now in those days a decree went out from Caesar Au·gusʹtus for all the inhabited earth to be registered.

25079.label: Luke 2:2
25079.text: (This first registration took place when Qui·rinʹi·us was governor of Syria.)

25080.label: Luke 2:3
25080.text: And all the people went to be registered, each one to his own city.

25081.label: Luke 2:4
25081.text: Of course, Joseph also went up from Galʹi·lee, from the city of Nazʹa·reth, into Ju·deʹa, to David’s city, which is called Bethʹle·hem, because of his being a member of the house and family of David.

25082.label: Luke 2:5
25082.text: He went to get registered with Mary, who had been given him in marriage as promised and who was soon to give birth.

25083.label: Luke 2:6
25083.text: While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.

25084.label: Luke 2:7
25084.text: And she gave birth to her son, the firstborn, and she wrapped him in strips of cloth and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the lodging place.

25085.label: Luke 2:8
25085.text: There were also in the same region shepherds living out of doors and keeping watch in the night over their flocks.

25086.label: Luke 2:9
25086.text: Suddenly Jehovah’s angel stood before them, and Jehovah’s glory gleamed around them, and they became very fearful.

25087.label: Luke 2:10
25087.text: But the angel said to them: “Do not be afraid, for look! I am declaring to you good news of a great joy that all the people will have.

25088.label: Luke 2:11
25088.text: For today there was born to you in David’s city a savior, who is Christ the Lord.

25089.label: Luke 2:12
25089.text: And this is a sign for you: You will find an infant wrapped in strips of cloth and lying in a manger.”

25090.label: Luke 2:13
25090.text: Suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying:

25091.label: Luke 2:14
25091.text: “Glory in the heights above to God, and on earth peace among men of goodwill.”

25092.label: Luke 2:15
25092.text: So when the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds began saying to one another: “Let us by all means go over to Bethʹle·hem and see what has taken place, which Jehovah has made known to us.”

25093.label: Luke 2:16
25093.text: And they went quickly and found Mary as well as Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.

25094.label: Luke 2:17
25094.text: When they saw this, they made known the message that they had been told concerning this young child.

25095.label: Luke 2:18
25095.text: And all who heard were astonished at what the shepherds told them,

25096.label: Luke 2:19
25096.text: but Mary began to preserve all these sayings, drawing conclusions in her heart.

25097.label: Luke 2:20
25097.text: Then the shepherds went back, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.

25098.label: Luke 2:21
25098.text: After eight days, when it was time to circumcise him, he was named Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived.

25099.label: Luke 2:22
25099.text: Also, when the time came for purifying them according to the Law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to Jehovah,

25100.label: Luke 2:23
25100.text: just as it is written in Jehovah’s Law: “Every firstborn male must be called holy to Jehovah.”

25101.label: Luke 2:24
25101.text: And they offered a sacrifice according to what is said in the Law of Jehovah: “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”

25102.label: Luke 2:25
25102.text: And look! there was a man in Jerusalem named Simʹe·on, and this man was righteous and devout, waiting for Israel’s consolation, and holy spirit was upon him.

25103.label: Luke 2:26
25103.text: Furthermore, it had been divinely revealed to him by the holy spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Christ of Jehovah.

25104.label: Luke 2:27
25104.text: Under the power of the spirit, he now came into the temple, and as the parents brought the young child Jesus in to do for him according to the customary practice of the Law,

25105.label: Luke 2:28
25105.text: he took the child into his arms and praised God and said:

25106.label: Luke 2:29
25106.text: “Now, Sovereign Lord, you are letting your slave go in peace according to your declaration,

25107.label: Luke 2:30
25107.text: because my eyes have seen your means of salvation

25108.label: Luke 2:31
25108.text: that you have prepared in the sight of all the peoples,

25109.label: Luke 2:32
25109.text: a light for removing the veil from the nations and a glory of your people Israel.”

25110.label: Luke 2:33
25110.text: And the child’s father and mother continued wondering at the things being spoken about him.

25111.label: Luke 2:34
25111.text: Also, Simʹe·on blessed them and said to Mary, the child’s mother: “Look! This child is appointed for the falling and the rising again of many in Israel and for a sign to be spoken against

25112.label: Luke 2:35
25112.text: (yes, a long sword will be run through you), in order that the reasonings of many hearts may be revealed.”

25113.label: Luke 2:36
25113.text: Now there was a prophetess, Anna the daughter of Phanʹu·el, of Ashʹer’s tribe. This woman was well along in years and had lived with her husband for seven years after they were married,

25114.label: Luke 2:37
25114.text: and she was a widow now 84 years old. She was never missing from the temple, rendering sacred service night and day with fasting and supplications.

25115.label: Luke 2:38
25115.text: In that very hour she came near and began giving thanks to God and speaking about the child to all who were waiting for Jerusalem’s deliverance.

25116.label: Luke 2:39
25116.text: So when they had carried out all the things according to the Law of Jehovah, they went back into Galʹi·lee to their own city, Nazʹa·reth.

25117.label: Luke 2:40
25117.text: And the young child continued growing and getting strong, being filled with wisdom, and God’s favor continued upon him.

25118.label: Luke 2:41
25118.text: Now his parents were accustomed to go from year to year to Jerusalem for the festival of the Passover.

25119.label: Luke 2:42
25119.text: And when he was 12 years old, they went up according to the custom of the festival.

25120.label: Luke 2:43
25120.text: When the days of the festival were over and they were returning, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, and his parents did not notice it.

25121.label: Luke 2:44
25121.text: Assuming that he was in the group traveling together, they went a day’s journey and then began to search for him among the relatives and acquaintances.

25122.label: Luke 2:45
25122.text: But not finding him, they returned to Jerusalem and made a diligent search for him.

25123.label: Luke 2:46
25123.text: Well, after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers and listening to them and asking them questions.

25124.label: Luke 2:47
25124.text: But all those listening to him were in constant amazement at his understanding and his answers.

25125.label: Luke 2:48
25125.text: Now when his parents saw him, they were astounded, and his mother said to him: “Child, why did you treat us this way? Here your father and I have been frantically looking for you.”

25126.label: Luke 2:49
25126.text: But he said to them: “Why were you looking for me? Did you not know that I must be in the house of my Father?”

25127.label: Luke 2:50
25127.text: However, they did not understand what he was saying to them.

25128.label: Luke 2:51
25128.text: Then he went down with them and returned to Nazʹa·reth, and he continued subject to them. Also, his mother carefully kept all these sayings in her heart.

25129.label: Luke 2:52
25129.text: And Jesus went on progressing in wisdom and in physical growth and in favor with God and men.

25130.label: Luke 3:1
25130.text: In the 15th year of the reign of Ti·beʹri·us Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Ju·deʹa, Herod was district ruler of Galʹi·lee, Philip his brother was district ruler of the country of It·u·raeʹa and Trach·o·niʹtis, and Ly·saʹni·as was district ruler of Ab·i·leʹne,

25131.label: Luke 3:2
25131.text: in the days of chief priest Anʹnas and of Caʹia·phas, God’s declaration came to John the son of Zech·a·riʹah in the wilderness.

25132.label: Luke 3:3
25132.text: So he went into all the country around the Jordan, preaching baptism in symbol of repentance for forgiveness of sins,

25133.label: Luke 3:4
25133.text: just as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of Jehovah! Make his roads straight.

25134.label: Luke 3:5
25134.text: Every valley must be filled up, and every mountain and hill leveled; the crooked ways must become straight, and the rough ways smooth;

25135.label: Luke 3:6
25135.text: and all flesh will see the salvation of God.’”

25136.label: Luke 3:7
25136.text: So he began to say to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him: “You offspring of vipers, who has warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

25137.label: Luke 3:8
25137.text: Therefore, produce fruits that befit repentance. Do not start saying to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I say to you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones.

25138.label: Luke 3:9
25138.text: Indeed, the ax is already lying at the root of the trees. Every tree, then, that does not produce fine fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”

25139.label: Luke 3:10
25139.text: And the crowds were asking him: “What, then, should we do?”

25140.label: Luke 3:11
25140.text: In reply he said to them: “Let the man who has two garments share with the man who has none, and let the one who has something to eat do the same.”

25141.label: Luke 3:12
25141.text: Even tax collectors came to be baptized, and they said to him: “Teacher, what should we do?”

25142.label: Luke 3:13
25142.text: He said to them: “Do not demand anything more than the tax rate.”

25143.label: Luke 3:14
25143.text: Also, those in military service were asking him: “What should we do?” And he said to them: “Do not harass anybody or accuse anybody falsely, but be satisfied with your provisions.”

25144.label: Luke 3:15
25144.text: Now the people were in expectation and all of them were reasoning in their hearts about John, “May he perhaps be the Christ?”

25145.label: Luke 3:16
25145.text: John gave the answer, saying to all: “I, for my part, baptize you with water, but the one stronger than I am is coming, the lace of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with holy spirit and with fire.

25146.label: Luke 3:17
25146.text: His winnowing shovel is in his hand to clean up his threshing floor completely and to gather the wheat into his storehouse, but the chaff he will burn up with fire that cannot be put out.”

25147.label: Luke 3:18
25147.text: He also gave many other exhortations and continued declaring good news to the people.

25148.label: Luke 3:19
25148.text: But Herod the district ruler, because of being reproved by John concerning He·roʹdi·as the wife of his brother and concerning all the wicked deeds that Herod had done,

25149.label: Luke 3:20
25149.text: added this also to all those deeds: He locked John up in prison.

25150.label: Luke 3:21
25150.text: Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus too was baptized. As he was praying, the heaven was opened up,

25151.label: Luke 3:22
25151.text: and the holy spirit in bodily form like a dove came down upon him, and a voice came out of heaven: “You are my Son, the beloved; I have approved you.”

25152.label: Luke 3:23
25152.text: When Jesus began his work, he was about 30 years old, being the son, as the opinion was,of Joseph, son of Heʹli,

25153.label: Luke 3:24
25153.text: son of Matʹthat,son of Leʹvi,son of Melʹchi,son of Janʹna·i,son of Joseph,

25154.label: Luke 3:25
25154.text: son of Mat·ta·thiʹas,son of Aʹmos,son of Naʹhum,son of Esʹli,son of Nagʹga·i,

25155.label: Luke 3:26
25155.text: son of Maʹath,son of Mat·ta·thiʹas,son of Semʹe·in,son of Joʹsech,son of Joʹda,

25156.label: Luke 3:27
25156.text: son of Jo·anʹan,son of Rheʹsa,son of Ze·rubʹba·bel, son of She·alʹti·el, son of Neʹri,

25157.label: Luke 3:28
25157.text: son of Melʹchi,son of Adʹdi,son of Coʹsam,son of El·maʹdam,son of Er,

25158.label: Luke 3:29
25158.text: son of Jesus,son of E·li·eʹzer,son of Joʹrim,son of Matʹthat,son of Leʹvi,

25159.label: Luke 3:30
25159.text: son of Symʹe·on,son of Judas,son of Joseph,son of Joʹnam,son of E·liʹa·kim,

25160.label: Luke 3:31
25160.text: son of Meʹle·a,son of Menʹna,son of Matʹta·tha,son of Nathan, son of David,

25161.label: Luke 3:32
25161.text: son of Jesʹse, son of Oʹbed, son of Boʹaz, son of Salʹmon, son of Nahʹshon,

25162.label: Luke 3:33
25162.text: son of Am·minʹa·dab, son of Arʹni,son of Hezʹron, son of Peʹrez, son of Judah,

25163.label: Luke 3:34
25163.text: son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Teʹrah, son of Naʹhor,

25164.label: Luke 3:35
25164.text: son of Seʹrug, son of Reʹu, son of Peʹleg, son of Eʹber, son of Sheʹlah,

25165.label: Luke 3:36
25165.text: son of Ca·iʹnan,son of Ar·pachʹshad, son of Shem, son of Noah, son of Laʹmech,

25166.label: Luke 3:37
25166.text: son of Me·thuʹse·lah, son of Eʹnoch, son of Jaʹred, son of Ma·haʹla·le·el, son of Ca·iʹnan,

25167.label: Luke 3:38
25167.text: son of Eʹnosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.

25168.label: Luke 4:1
25168.text: Then Jesus, full of holy spirit, turned away from the Jordan, and he was led about by the spirit in the wilderness

25169.label: Luke 4:2
25169.text: for 40 days, being tempted by the Devil. And he ate nothing in those days, so when they had ended, he felt hungry.

25170.label: Luke 4:3
25170.text: At this the Devil said to him: “If you are a son of God, tell this stone to become a loaf of bread.”

25171.label: Luke 4:4
25171.text: But Jesus answered him: “It is written, ‘Man must not live on bread alone.’”

25172.label: Luke 4:5
25172.text: So he brought him up and showed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited earth in an instant of time.

25173.label: Luke 4:6
25173.text: Then the Devil said to him: “I will give you all this authority and their glory, because it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.

25174.label: Luke 4:7
25174.text: If you, therefore, do an act of worship before me, it will all be yours.”

25175.label: Luke 4:8
25175.text: In reply Jesus said to him: “It is written, ‘It is Jehovah your God you must worship, and it is to him alone you must render sacred service.’”

25176.label: Luke 4:9
25176.text: He then led him into Jerusalem and stationed him on the battlement of the temple and said to him: “If you are a son of God, throw yourself down from here,

25177.label: Luke 4:10
25177.text: for it is written, ‘He will give his angels a command concerning you, to preserve you,’

25178.label: Luke 4:11
25178.text: and, ‘They will carry you on their hands, so that you may not strike your foot against a stone.’”

25179.label: Luke 4:12
25179.text: In answer Jesus said to him: “It is said, ‘You must not put Jehovah your God to the test.’”

25180.label: Luke 4:13
25180.text: So the Devil, having finished all the temptation, departed from him until another convenient time.

25181.label: Luke 4:14
25181.text: Now Jesus returned in the power of the spirit into Galʹi·lee. And good reports about him spread throughout all the surrounding country.

25182.label: Luke 4:15
25182.text: Also, he began to teach in their synagogues, and he was held in honor by all.

25183.label: Luke 4:16
25183.text: He then went to Nazʹa·reth, where he had been brought up, and according to his custom on the Sabbath day, he entered the synagogue and stood up to read.

25184.label: Luke 4:17
25184.text: So the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him, and he opened the scroll and found the place where it was written:

25185.label: Luke 4:18
25185.text: “Jehovah’s spirit is upon me, because he anointed me to declare good news to the poor. He sent me to proclaim liberty to the captives and a recovery of sight to the blind, to send the crushed ones away free,

25187.label: Luke 4:20
25187.text: With that he rolled up the scroll, handed it back to the attendant, and sat down; and the eyes of all in the synagogue were intently fixed on him.

25188.label: Luke 4:21
25188.text: Then he began to say to them: “Today this scripture that you just heard is fulfilled.”

25189.label: Luke 4:22
25189.text: And they all began to give favorable witness about him and to be amazed at the gracious words coming out of his mouth, and they were saying: “This is a son of Joseph, is it not?”

25190.label: Luke 4:23
25190.text: At this he said to them: “No doubt you will apply this saying to me, ‘Physician, cure yourself. Do also here in your home territory the things we have heard were done in Ca·perʹna·um.’”

25191.label: Luke 4:24
25191.text: So he said: “Truly I tell you that no prophet is accepted in his home territory.

25192.label: Luke 4:25
25192.text: For instance, I tell you in truth: There were many widows in Israel in the days of E·liʹjah when heaven was shut up for three years and six months, and a great famine came on all the land.

25193.label: Luke 4:26
25193.text: Yet E·liʹjah was sent to none of those women, but only to a widow in Zarʹe·phath in the land of Siʹdon.

25194.label: Luke 4:27
25194.text: Also, there were many lepers in Israel in the time of E·liʹsha the prophet; yet not one of them was cleansed, only Naʹa·man the Syrian.”

25195.label: Luke 4:28
25195.text: Now all those hearing these things in the synagogue became filled with anger,

25196.label: Luke 4:29
25196.text: and they rose up and rushed him outside the city, and they led him to the brow of the mountain on which their city had been built, in order to throw him down headlong.

25197.label: Luke 4:30
25197.text: But he went right through their midst and continued on his way.

25198.label: Luke 4:31
25198.text: He then went down to Ca·perʹna·um, a city of Galʹi·lee. And he was teaching them on the Sabbath,

25199.label: Luke 4:32
25199.text: and they were astounded at his way of teaching, because he spoke with authority.

25200.label: Luke 4:33
25200.text: Now in the synagogue there was a man with a spirit, an unclean demon, and he shouted with a loud voice:

25201.label: Luke 4:34
25201.text: “Ah! What have we to do with you, Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ? Did you come to destroy us? I know exactly who you are, the Holy One of God.”

25202.label: Luke 4:35
25202.text: But Jesus rebuked it, saying: “Be silent, and come out of him.” So after throwing the man down in their midst, the demon came out of him without hurting him.

25203.label: Luke 4:36
25203.text: At this they were all astonished and began to say to one another: “What kind of speech is this? For with authority and power he orders the unclean spirits, and out they come!”

25204.label: Luke 4:37
25204.text: So the news about him kept spreading into every corner of the surrounding country.

25205.label: Luke 4:38
25205.text: After leaving the synagogue, he entered into Simon’s home. Now Simon’s mother-in-law was suffering with a high fever, and they asked him to help her.

25206.label: Luke 4:39
25206.text: So he stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. Instantly she got up and began ministering to them.

25207.label: Luke 4:40
25207.text: But when the sun was setting, all those who had people sick with various diseases brought them to him. By laying his hands on each one of them, he cured them.

25208.label: Luke 4:41
25208.text: Demons also came out of many, crying out and saying: “You are the Son of God.” But rebuking them, he would not permit them to speak, for they knew him to be the Christ.

25209.label: Luke 4:42
25209.text: However, at daybreak he departed and went to an isolated place. But the crowds began searching for him and came to where he was, and they tried to keep him from going away from them.

25210.label: Luke 4:43
25210.text: But he said to them: “I must also declare the good news of the Kingdom of God to other cities, because for this I was sent.”

25211.label: Luke 4:44
25211.text: So he went on preaching in the synagogues of Ju·deʹa.

25212.label: Luke 5:1
25212.text: On one occasion when the crowd was pressing in on him and listening to the word of God, he was standing by the lake of Gen·nesʹa·ret.

25213.label: Luke 5:2
25213.text: And he saw two boats docked at the lakeside, but the fishermen had got out of them and were washing off their nets.

25214.label: Luke 5:3
25214.text: Going aboard one of the boats, which was Simon’s, he asked him to pull away a bit from land. Then he sat down, and he began teaching the crowds from the boat.

25215.label: Luke 5:4
25215.text: When he stopped speaking, he said to Simon: “Pull out to where it is deep, and let down your nets for a catch.”

25216.label: Luke 5:5
25216.text: But in reply Simon said: “Instructor, we toiled all night and caught nothing, but at your word I will lower the nets.”

25217.label: Luke 5:6
25217.text: Well, when they did this, they caught a great number of fish. In fact, their nets began ripping apart.

25218.label: Luke 5:7
25218.text: So they motioned to their partners in the other boat to come and assist them, and they came and filled both boats, so that these began to sink.

25219.label: Luke 5:8
25219.text: Seeing this, Simon Peter fell down at the knees of Jesus, saying: “Depart from me, Lord, because I am a sinful man.”

25220.label: Luke 5:9
25220.text: For both he and those with him were overwhelmed with astonishment at the catch of fish they had taken,

25221.label: Luke 5:10
25221.text: and the same was true of both James and John, Zebʹe·dee’s sons, who were partners with Simon. But Jesus said to Simon: “Stop being afraid. From now on you will be catching men alive.”

25222.label: Luke 5:11
25222.text: So they brought the boats back to land and abandoned everything and followed him.

25223.label: Luke 5:12
25223.text: On another occasion while he was in one of the cities, look! there was a man full of leprosy! When he caught sight of Jesus, he fell facedown and begged him: “Lord, if you just want to, you can make me clean.”

25224.label: Luke 5:13
25224.text: So stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying: “I want to! Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy vanished from him.

25225.label: Luke 5:14
25225.text: Then he gave the man orders to tell no one: “But go and show yourself to the priest, and make an offering for your cleansing, just as Moses directed, for a witness to them.”

25226.label: Luke 5:15
25226.text: But the news about him just kept spreading, and large crowds would gather together to listen and to be cured of their sicknesses.

25227.label: Luke 5:16
25227.text: However, he often went into the desolate areas to pray.

25228.label: Luke 5:17
25228.text: On one of those days while he was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the Law who had come out of every village of Galʹi·lee and Ju·deʹa and from Jerusalem were sitting there; and Jehovah’s power was with him to do healing.

25229.label: Luke 5:18
25229.text: And look! men were carrying a paralyzed man on a stretcher, and they were trying to bring him in and place him before Jesus.

25230.label: Luke 5:19
25230.text: So not finding a way to bring him in because of the crowd, they climbed up to the roof, and they lowered him on the stretcher through the tiling, right among those in front of Jesus.

25231.label: Luke 5:20
25231.text: When he saw their faith, he said: “Man, your sins are forgiven.”

25232.label: Luke 5:21
25232.text: Then the scribes and the Pharisees started to reason, saying: “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”

25233.label: Luke 5:22
25233.text: But Jesus, discerning their reasoning, said in answer to them: “What are you reasoning in your hearts?

25234.label: Luke 5:23
25234.text: Which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?

25235.label: Luke 5:24
25235.text: But in order for you to know that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins—” he said to the paralyzed man: “I say to you, Get up, pick up your stretcher, and go to your home.”

25236.label: Luke 5:25
25236.text: At that he stood up before them, picked up what he had been lying on, and went to his home, glorifying God.

25237.label: Luke 5:26
25237.text: Then one and all were seized with amazement, and they began to glorify God, and they became filled with awe, saying: “We have seen wonderful things today!”

25238.label: Luke 5:27
25238.text: Now after this, he went out and saw a tax collector named Leʹvi sitting at the tax office, and he said to him: “Be my follower.”

25239.label: Luke 5:28
25239.text: And leaving everything behind, he rose up and began to follow him.

25240.label: Luke 5:29
25240.text: Then Leʹvi spread a big reception feast for him in his house, and there was a large crowd of tax collectors and others who were dining with them.

25241.label: Luke 5:30
25241.text: At this the Pharisees and their scribes began murmuring to his disciples, saying: “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”

25242.label: Luke 5:31
25242.text: In reply Jesus said to them: “Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those who are ill do.

25243.label: Luke 5:32
25243.text: I have come to call, not righteous people, but sinners to repentance.”

25244.label: Luke 5:33
25244.text: They said to him: “John’s disciples fast frequently and offer supplications, and so do those of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink.”

25245.label: Luke 5:34
25245.text: Jesus said to them: “You cannot make the friends of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them, can you?

25246.label: Luke 5:35
25246.text: But days will come when the bridegroom will indeed be taken away from them; then they will fast in those days.”

25247.label: Luke 5:36
25247.text: He also gave an illustration to them: “Nobody cuts a patch from a new outer garment and sews it on an old garment. If he does, then the new patch tears away and the patch from the new garment does not match the old.

25248.label: Luke 5:37
25248.text: Also, no one puts new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the wineskins and it will be spilled out and the wineskins will be ruined.

25249.label: Luke 5:38
25249.text: But new wine must be put into new wineskins.

25250.label: Luke 5:39
25250.text: No one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is nice.’”

25251.label: Luke 6:1
25251.text: Now on a sabbath he was passing through grainfields, and his disciples were plucking and eating the heads of grain, rubbing them with their hands.

25252.label: Luke 6:2
25252.text: At this some of the Pharisees said: “Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”

25253.label: Luke 6:3
25253.text: But in reply Jesus said to them: “Have you never read what David did when he and the men with him were hungry?

25254.label: Luke 6:4
25254.text: How he entered into the house of God and received the loaves of presentation and ate and gave some to the men with him, which it is not lawful for anyone to eat but for the priests only?”

25255.label: Luke 6:5
25255.text: Then he said to them: “The Son of man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

25256.label: Luke 6:6
25256.text: On another sabbath he entered the synagogue and began teaching. And a man was there whose right hand was withered.

25257.label: Luke 6:7
25257.text: The scribes and the Pharisees were now watching Jesus closely to see whether he would cure on the Sabbath, in order to find some way to accuse him.

25258.label: Luke 6:8
25258.text: He, however, knew their reasoning, so he said to the man with the withered hand: “Get up and stand in the center.” And he rose and stood there.

25259.label: Luke 6:9
25259.text: Then Jesus said to them: “I ask you men, Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to destroy it?”

25260.label: Luke 6:10
25260.text: After looking around at them all, he said to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and his hand was restored.

25261.label: Luke 6:11
25261.text: But they flew into a senseless rage, and they began to talk over with one another what they might do to Jesus.

25262.label: Luke 6:12
25262.text: On one of those days he went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the whole night in prayer to God.

25263.label: Luke 6:13
25263.text: And when it became day, he called his disciples to him and chose from among them 12, whom he also named apostles:

25264.label: Luke 6:14
25264.text: Simon, whom he also named Peter, Andrew his brother, James, John, Philip, Bar·tholʹo·mew,

25265.label: Luke 6:15
25265.text: Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Al·phaeʹus, Simon who is called “the zealous one,”

25266.label: Luke 6:16
25266.text: Judas the son of James, and Judas Is·carʹi·ot, who turned traitor.

25267.label: Luke 6:17
25267.text: And he came down with them and stood on a level place, and there was a large crowd of his disciples, and a great multitude of people from all Ju·deʹa and Jerusalem and the coastal region of Tyre and Siʹdon, who came to hear him and to be healed of their sicknesses.

25268.label: Luke 6:18
25268.text: Even those troubled with unclean spirits were cured.

25269.label: Luke 6:19
25269.text: And all the crowd were seeking to touch him, because power was going out of him and healing them all.

25270.label: Luke 6:20
25270.text: And he looked up at his disciples and began to say: “Happy are you who are poor, for yours is the Kingdom of God.

25271.label: Luke 6:21
25271.text: “Happy are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. “Happy are you who weep now, for you will laugh.

25272.label: Luke 6:22
25272.text: “Happy are you whenever men hate you, and when they exclude you and reproach you and denounce your name as wicked for the sake of the Son of man.

25273.label: Luke 6:23
25273.text: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for look! your reward is great in heaven, for those are the same things their forefathers used to do to the prophets.

25274.label: Luke 6:24
25274.text: “But woe to you who are rich, for you are having your consolation in full.

25275.label: Luke 6:25
25275.text: “Woe to you who are filled up now, for you will go hungry. “Woe, you who are laughing now, for you will mourn and weep.

25276.label: Luke 6:26
25276.text: “Woe whenever all men speak well of you, for this is what their forefathers did to the false prophets.

25277.label: Luke 6:27
25277.text: “But I say to you who are listening: Continue to love your enemies, to do good to those hating you,

25278.label: Luke 6:28
25278.text: to bless those cursing you, to pray for those who are insulting you.

25279.label: Luke 6:29
25279.text: To him who strikes you on the one cheek, offer the other also; and from him who takes away your outer garment, do not withhold the inner garment either.

25280.label: Luke 6:30
25280.text: Give to everyone asking you, and from the one taking your things away, do not ask them back.

25281.label: Luke 6:31
25281.text: “Also, just as you want men to do to you, do the same way to them.

25282.label: Luke 6:32
25282.text: “If you love those loving you, of what credit is it to you? For even the sinners love those loving them.

25283.label: Luke 6:33
25283.text: And if you do good to those doing good to you, of what credit is it to you? Even the sinners do the same.

25284.label: Luke 6:34
25284.text: Also, if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, of what credit is it to you? Even sinners lend to sinners so that they may get back as much.

25285.label: Luke 6:35
25285.text: On the contrary, continue to love your enemies and to do good and to lend without hoping for anything back; and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for he is kind toward the unthankful and wicked.

25286.label: Luke 6:36
25286.text: Continue being merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

25287.label: Luke 6:37
25287.text: “Moreover, stop judging, and you will by no means be judged; and stop condemning, and you will by no means be condemned. Keep on forgiving, and you will be forgiven.

25288.label: Luke 6:38
25288.text: Practice giving, and people will give to you. They will pour into your laps a fine measure, pressed down, shaken together, and overflowing. For with the measure that you are measuring out, they will measure out to you in return.”

25289.label: Luke 6:39
25289.text: Then he also told them an illustration: “A blind man cannot guide a blind man, can he? Both will fall into a pit, will they not?

25290.label: Luke 6:40
25290.text: A student is not above his teacher, but everyone who is perfectly instructed will be like his teacher.

25291.label: Luke 6:41
25291.text: Why, then, do you look at the straw in your brother’s eye but do not notice the rafter in your own eye?

25292.label: Luke 6:42
25292.text: How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, allow me to remove the straw that is in your eye,’ while you yourself do not see the rafter in your own eye? Hypocrite! First remove the rafter from your own eye, and then you will see clearly how to remove the straw that is in your brother’s eye.

25293.label: Luke 6:43
25293.text: “For no fine tree produces rotten fruit, and no rotten tree produces fine fruit.

25294.label: Luke 6:44
25294.text: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For example, people do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they cut grapes off a thornbush.

25295.label: Luke 6:45
25295.text: A good man brings good out of the good treasure of his heart, but a wicked man brings what is wicked out of his wicked treasure; for out of the heart’s abundance his mouth speaks.

25296.label: Luke 6:46
25296.text: “Why, then, do you call me ‘Lord! Lord!’ but do not do the things I say?

25297.label: Luke 6:47
25297.text: Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you whom he is like:

25298.label: Luke 6:48
25298.text: He is like a man who in building a house dug and went down deep and laid a foundation on the rock. Consequently, when a flood came, the river dashed against that house but was not strong enough to shake it, for it was well-built.

25299.label: Luke 6:49
25299.text: On the other hand, whoever hears and does nothing is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. The river dashed against it, and immediately it collapsed, and the ruin of that house was great.”

25300.label: Luke 7:1
25300.text: When he had completed what he had to say to the people, he entered Ca·perʹna·um.

25301.label: Luke 7:2
25301.text: Now an army officer’s slave, who was dear to him, was seriously ill and about to pass away.

25302.label: Luke 7:3
25302.text: When he heard about Jesus, he sent some elders of the Jews to him to ask him to come and make his slave well.

25303.label: Luke 7:4
25303.text: They came up to Jesus and began to plead with him earnestly, saying: “He is worthy of your granting him this,

25304.label: Luke 7:5
25304.text: for he loves our nation and he himself built our synagogue.”

25305.label: Luke 7:6
25305.text: So Jesus went with them. But when he was not far from the house, the army officer had already sent friends to say to him: “Sir, do not bother, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof.

25306.label: Luke 7:7
25306.text: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and let my servant be healed.

25307.label: Luke 7:8
25307.text: For I too am a man placed under authority, having soldiers under me, and I say to this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes, and to my slave, ‘Do this!’ and he does it.”

25308.label: Luke 7:9
25308.text: When Jesus heard these things, he was amazed at him, and he turned to the crowd following him and said: “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found so great a faith.”

25309.label: Luke 7:10
25309.text: And when those who had been sent returned to the house, they found the slave in good health.

25310.label: Luke 7:11
25310.text: Soon afterward he traveled to a city called Naʹin, and his disciples and a large crowd were traveling with him.

25311.label: Luke 7:12
25311.text: As he got near the gate of the city, why look! there was a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother. Besides, she was a widow. A considerable crowd from the city was also with her.

25312.label: Luke 7:13
25312.text: When the Lord caught sight of her, he was moved with pity for her, and he said to her: “Stop weeping.”

25313.label: Luke 7:14
25313.text: With that he approached and touched the bier, and the bearers stood still. Then he said: “Young man, I say to you, get up!”

25314.label: Luke 7:15
25314.text: And the dead man sat up and started to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother.

25315.label: Luke 7:16
25315.text: Now fear seized them all, and they began to glorify God, saying: “A great prophet has been raised up among us,” and, “God has turned his attention to his people.”

25316.label: Luke 7:17
25316.text: And this news concerning him spread out into all Ju·deʹa and all the surrounding country.

25317.label: Luke 7:18
25317.text: Now John’s disciples reported to him all these things.

25318.label: Luke 7:19
25318.text: So John summoned two of his disciples and sent them to the Lord to ask: “Are you the Coming One, or are we to expect a different one?”

25319.label: Luke 7:20
25319.text: When they came to him, the men said: “John the Baptist sent us to you to ask, ‘Are you the Coming One, or are we to expect another?’”

25320.label: Luke 7:21
25320.text: In that hour he cured many people of sicknesses, serious diseases, and wicked spirits, and he granted many blind people the gift of sight.

25321.label: Luke 7:22
25321.text: In reply he said to them: “Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind are now seeing, the lame are walking, the lepers are being cleansed, the deaf are hearing, the dead are being raised up, and the poor are being told the good news.

25322.label: Luke 7:23
25322.text: Happy is the one who finds no cause for stumbling in me.”

25323.label: Luke 7:24
25323.text: When the messengers of John had gone away, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed being tossed by the wind?

25324.label: Luke 7:25
25324.text: What, then, did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft garments? Why, those wearing splendid dress and living in luxury are in royal houses.

25325.label: Luke 7:26
25325.text: Really, then, what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and far more than a prophet.

25326.label: Luke 7:27
25326.text: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Look! I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way ahead of you.’

25327.label: Luke 7:28
25327.text: I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John, but a lesser person in the Kingdom of God is greater than he is.”

25328.label: Luke 7:29
25328.text: (When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they declared God to be righteous, for they had been baptized with the baptism of John.

25329.label: Luke 7:30
25329.text: But the Pharisees and those versed in the Law disregarded the counsel of God to them, since they had not been baptized by him.)

25330.label: Luke 7:31
25330.text: “With whom, therefore, should I compare the men of this generation, and whom are they like?

25331.label: Luke 7:32
25331.text: They are like young children sitting in a marketplace and calling out to one another, saying: ‘We played the flute for you, but you did not dance; we wailed, but you did not weep.’

25332.label: Luke 7:33
25332.text: Likewise, John the Baptist has come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, but you say: ‘He has a demon.’

25333.label: Luke 7:34
25333.text: The Son of man has come eating and drinking, but you say: ‘Look! A man who is a glutton and is given to drinking wine, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

25334.label: Luke 7:35
25334.text: All the same, wisdom is proved righteous by all its children.”

25335.label: Luke 7:36
25335.text: Now one of the Pharisees kept asking him to dine with him. So he entered the house of the Pharisee and reclined at the table.

25336.label: Luke 7:37
25336.text: And look! a woman who was known in the city to be a sinner learned that he was dining in the house of the Pharisee, and she brought an alabaster jar of perfumed oil.

25337.label: Luke 7:38
25337.text: Taking a position behind him at his feet, she wept and began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them off with the hair of her head. Also, she tenderly kissed his feet and poured the perfumed oil on them.

25338.label: Luke 7:39
25338.text: Seeing this, the Pharisee who had invited him said to himself: “If this man were really a prophet, he would know who and what kind of woman it is who is touching him, that she is a sinner.”

25339.label: Luke 7:40
25339.text: But in reply Jesus said to him: “Simon, I have something to say to you.” He said: “Teacher, say it!”

25340.label: Luke 7:41
25340.text: “Two men were debtors to a certain lender; the one was in debt for 500 de·narʹi·i, but the other for 50.

25341.label: Luke 7:42
25341.text: When they did not have anything to pay him back with, he freely forgave them both. Therefore, which one of them will love him more?”

25342.label: Luke 7:43
25342.text: In answer Simon said: “I suppose it is the one whom he forgave more.” He said to him: “You judged correctly.”

25343.label: Luke 7:44
25343.text: With that he turned to the woman and said to Simon: “Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave me no water for my feet. But this woman wet my feet with her tears and wiped them off with her hair.

25344.label: Luke 7:45
25344.text: You gave me no kiss, but this woman, from the hour that I came in, did not stop tenderly kissing my feet.

25345.label: Luke 7:46
25345.text: You did not pour oil on my head, but this woman poured perfumed oil on my feet.

25346.label: Luke 7:47
25346.text: Because of this, I tell you, her sins, many though they are, are forgiven, because she loved much. But the one who is forgiven little, loves little.”

25347.label: Luke 7:48
25347.text: Then he said to her: “Your sins are forgiven.”

25348.label: Luke 7:49
25348.text: Those reclining at the table with him started to say among themselves: “Who is this man who even forgives sins?”

25349.label: Luke 7:50
25349.text: But he said to the woman: “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

25350.label: Luke 8:1
25350.text: Shortly afterward he traveled from city to city and from village to village, preaching and declaring the good news of the Kingdom of God. And the Twelve were with him,

25351.label: Luke 8:2
25351.text: as were certain women who had been cured of wicked spirits and sicknesses: Mary who was called Magʹda·lene, from whom seven demons had come out;

25352.label: Luke 8:3
25352.text: Jo·anʹna the wife of Chuʹza, Herod’s man in charge; Su·sanʹna; and many other women, who were ministering to them from their belongings.

25353.label: Luke 8:4
25353.text: Now when a large crowd had gathered together with those who went to him from city to city, he spoke by means of an illustration:

25354.label: Luke 8:5
25354.text: “A sower went out to sow his seed. As he was sowing, some of them fell alongside the road and were trampled on, and the birds of heaven ate them up.

25355.label: Luke 8:6
25355.text: Some landed on the rock, and after sprouting, they dried up because they had no moisture.

25356.label: Luke 8:7
25356.text: Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns that grew up with them choked them.

25357.label: Luke 8:8
25357.text: But others fell on the good soil, and after sprouting, they produced 100 times more fruit.” As he said these things, he called out: “Let the one who has ears to listen, listen.”

25358.label: Luke 8:9
25358.text: But his disciples asked him what this illustration meant.

25359.label: Luke 8:10
25359.text: He said: “To you it is granted to understand the sacred secrets of the Kingdom of God, but for the rest it is in illustrations so that, though looking, they may look in vain, and though hearing, they may not get the sense.

25360.label: Luke 8:11
25360.text: Now the illustration means this: The seed is the word of God.

25361.label: Luke 8:12
25361.text: Those alongside the road are the ones who have heard, and then the Devil comes and takes the word away from their hearts so that they may not believe and be saved.

25362.label: Luke 8:13
25362.text: Those on the rock are the ones who, when they hear the word, receive it with joy, but these have no root. They believe for a while, but in a season of testing, they fall away.

25363.label: Luke 8:14
25363.text: As for that which fell among the thorns, these are the ones who have heard, but by being carried away by anxieties, riches, and pleasures of this life, they are completely choked and bring nothing to maturity.

25364.label: Luke 8:15
25364.text: As for that on the fine soil, these are the ones who, after hearing the word with a fine and good heart, retain it and bear fruit with endurance.

25365.label: Luke 8:16
25365.text: “No one after lighting a lamp covers it with a vessel or puts it underneath a bed, but he puts it on a lampstand so that those who come in may see the light.

25366.label: Luke 8:17
25366.text: For there is nothing hidden that will not become manifest, nor anything carefully concealed that will never become known and not come out in the open.

25367.label: Luke 8:18
25367.text: Therefore, pay attention to how you listen, for whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he imagines he has will be taken away from him.”

25368.label: Luke 8:19
25368.text: Now his mother and brothers came to him, but they were unable to get near him because of the crowd.

25369.label: Luke 8:20
25369.text: So it was reported to him: “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”

25370.label: Luke 8:21
25370.text: In reply he said to them: “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”

25371.label: Luke 8:22
25371.text: One day he and his disciples got into a boat, and he said to them: “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So they set sail.

25372.label: Luke 8:23
25372.text: But as they were sailing along, he fell asleep. And a violent windstorm descended on the lake, and their boat began to fill up with water and to be in danger.

25373.label: Luke 8:24
25373.text: So they went and woke him up, saying: “Instructor, Instructor, we are about to perish!” With that he got up and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and they subsided, and a calm set in.

25374.label: Luke 8:25
25374.text: Then he said to them: “Where is your faith?” But they were filled with fear and were astounded, saying to one another: “Who really is this? For he orders even the winds and the water, and they obey him.”

25375.label: Luke 8:26
25375.text: And they put in to shore in the region of the Gerʹa·senes, which is on the side opposite Galʹi·lee.

25376.label: Luke 8:27
25376.text: As Jesus got out onto land, a demon-possessed man from the city met him. For a considerable time he had not worn clothing, and he was staying, not in a house, but among the tombs.

25377.label: Luke 8:28
25377.text: At the sight of Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, and with a loud voice, he said: “What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me.”

25378.label: Luke 8:29
25378.text: (For Jesus had been ordering the unclean spirit to come out of the man. It had seized him on many occasions, and he was repeatedly bound with chains and fetters and kept under guard, but he would break the bonds and be driven by the demon into the isolated places.)

25379.label: Luke 8:30
25379.text: Jesus asked him: “What is your name?” He said: “Legion,” for many demons had entered into him.

25380.label: Luke 8:31
25380.text: And they kept pleading with him not to order them to go away into the abyss.

25381.label: Luke 8:32
25381.text: Now a large herd of swine was feeding there on the mountain, so they pleaded with him to permit them to enter into the swine, and he gave them permission.

25382.label: Luke 8:33
25382.text: With that the demons came out of the man and went into the swine, and the herd rushed over the precipice into the lake and drowned.

25383.label: Luke 8:34
25383.text: But when the herders saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the city and in the countryside.

25384.label: Luke 8:35
25384.text: Then people went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had come out, clothed and in his right mind, sitting at the feet of Jesus, and they grew fearful.

25385.label: Luke 8:36
25385.text: Those who had seen it reported to them how the demon-possessed man had been made well.

25386.label: Luke 8:37
25386.text: Then a great number from the surrounding region of the Gerʹa·senes asked Jesus to go away from them, because they were gripped by great fear. Then he went aboard the boat to depart.

25387.label: Luke 8:38
25387.text: However, the man from whom the demons had gone out kept begging to continue with him, but he sent the man away, saying:

25388.label: Luke 8:39
25388.text: “Go back home, and keep on relating what God did for you.” So he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole city what Jesus had done for him.

25389.label: Luke 8:40
25389.text: When Jesus returned, the crowd received him kindly, for they were all expecting him.

25390.label: Luke 8:41
25390.text: But look! a man named Jaʹi·rus came; this man was a presiding officer of the synagogue. And he fell at the feet of Jesus and began to plead with him to come to his house,

25391.label: Luke 8:42
25391.text: because his only daughter, who was about 12 years old, was dying. As Jesus was going, the crowds pressed in on him.

25392.label: Luke 8:43
25392.text: Now there was a woman who had a flow of blood for 12 years, and she had not been able to get a cure from anyone.

25393.label: Luke 8:44
25393.text: She approached from behind and touched the fringe of his outer garment, and immediately her flow of blood stopped.

25394.label: Luke 8:45
25394.text: So Jesus said: “Who touched me?” When they were all denying it, Peter said: “Instructor, the crowds are hemming you in and pressing against you.”

25395.label: Luke 8:46
25395.text: But Jesus said: “Someone touched me, for I know that power went out of me.”

25396.label: Luke 8:47
25396.text: Seeing that she had not escaped notice, the woman came trembling and fell down before him and declared before all the people why she touched him and how she was healed immediately.

25397.label: Luke 8:48
25397.text: But he said to her: “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”

25398.label: Luke 8:49
25398.text: While he was yet speaking, a representative of the presiding officer of the synagogue came, saying: “Your daughter has died; do not bother the Teacher any longer.”

25399.label: Luke 8:50
25399.text: On hearing this, Jesus answered him: “Have no fear, only have faith, and she will be saved.”

25400.label: Luke 8:51
25400.text: When he reached the house, he did not let anyone go in with him except Peter, John, James, and the girl’s father and mother.

25401.label: Luke 8:52
25401.text: But people were all weeping and beating themselves in grief for her. So he said: “Stop weeping, for she did not die but is sleeping.”

25402.label: Luke 8:53
25402.text: At this they began to laugh at him scornfully, because they knew she had died.

25403.label: Luke 8:54
25403.text: But he took her by the hand and called to her: “Child, get up!”

25404.label: Luke 8:55
25404.text: And her spirit returned, and she rose immediately, and he ordered that something be given her to eat.

25405.label: Luke 8:56
25405.text: Well, her parents were beside themselves, but he instructed them to tell no one what had happened.

25406.label: Luke 9:1
25406.text: Then he called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all the demons and to cure diseases.

25407.label: Luke 9:2
25407.text: And he sent them out to preach the Kingdom of God and to heal,

25408.label: Luke 9:3
25408.text: and he said to them: “Carry nothing for the trip, neither staff nor food pouch nor bread nor money; neither have two garments.

25409.label: Luke 9:4
25409.text: But wherever you enter into a home, stay there and leave from there.

25410.label: Luke 9:5
25410.text: And wherever people do not receive you, on going out of that city, shake the dust off your feet for a witness against them.”

25411.label: Luke 9:6
25411.text: Then starting out, they went through the territory from village to village, declaring the good news and performing cures everywhere.

25412.label: Luke 9:7
25412.text: Now Herod the district ruler heard about everything that was happening, and he was greatly perplexed because some were saying that John had been raised up from the dead,

25413.label: Luke 9:8
25413.text: but others were saying that E·liʹjah had appeared, and still others that one of the ancient prophets had risen.

25414.label: Luke 9:9
25414.text: Herod said: “John I beheaded. Who, then, is this about whom I am hearing such things?” So he was trying to see him.

25415.label: Luke 9:10
25415.text: When the apostles returned, they reported to Jesus all they had done. With that he took them along and withdrew privately to a city called Beth·saʹi·da.

25416.label: Luke 9:11
25416.text: But the crowds, getting to know it, followed him. And he received them kindly and began to speak to them about the Kingdom of God, and he healed those needing a cure.

25417.label: Luke 9:12
25417.text: Then the day was coming to a close. The Twelve now came up and said to him: “Send the crowd away, so that they may go into the surrounding villages and countryside to find lodging and provisions, because out here we are in an isolated place.”

25418.label: Luke 9:13
25418.text: But he said to them: “You give them something to eat.” They said: “We have nothing more than five loaves and two fish, unless perhaps we ourselves go and buy food for all these people.”

25419.label: Luke 9:14
25419.text: There were, in fact, about 5,000 men. But he said to his disciples: “Have them sit down in groups of about 50 each.”

25420.label: Luke 9:15
25420.text: And they did so and had them all sit down.

25421.label: Luke 9:16
25421.text: Taking now the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven and blessed them. Then he broke them up and began giving them to the disciples to set before the crowd.

25422.label: Luke 9:17
25422.text: So they all ate and were satisfied, and they took up the leftovers, 12 baskets of fragments.

25423.label: Luke 9:18
25423.text: Later, while he was praying alone, the disciples came to him, and he questioned them, saying: “Who are the crowds saying that I am?”

25424.label: Luke 9:19
25424.text: In reply they said: “John the Baptist, but others say E·liʹjah, and still others say that one of the ancient prophets has risen.”

25425.label: Luke 9:20
25425.text: Then he said to them: “You, though, who do you say I am?” Peter answered: “The Christ of God.”

25426.label: Luke 9:21
25426.text: Then in a stern talk to them, he instructed them not to tell this to anybody,

25427.label: Luke 9:22
25427.text: but he said: “The Son of man must undergo many sufferings and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes and be killed, and on the third day be raised up.”

25428.label: Luke 9:23
25428.text: Then he went on to say to all: “If anyone wants to come after me, let him disown himself and pick up his torture stake day after day and keep following me.

25429.label: Luke 9:24
25429.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake is the one who will save it.

25430.label: Luke 9:25
25430.text: Really, what good will it do a man if he gains the whole world but loses his own self or suffers ruin?

25431.label: Luke 9:26
25431.text: For whoever becomes ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of man will be ashamed of that person when he comes in his glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels.

25432.label: Luke 9:27
25432.text: But I tell you truly, there are some of those standing here who will not taste death at all until first they see the Kingdom of God.”

25433.label: Luke 9:28
25433.text: In fact, about eight days after saying these words, he took Peter, John, and James along and climbed up the mountain to pray.

25434.label: Luke 9:29
25434.text: And as he was praying, the appearance of his face changed and his clothing became glitteringly white.

25435.label: Luke 9:30
25435.text: And look! two men were conversing with him; they were Moses and E·liʹjah.

25436.label: Luke 9:31
25436.text: These appeared with glory and began talking about his departure, which he was about to fulfill at Jerusalem.

25437.label: Luke 9:32
25437.text: Now Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep, but when they became fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

25438.label: Luke 9:33
25438.text: And as these were departing from him, Peter said to Jesus: “Instructor, it is fine for us to be here. So let us erect three tents, one for you, one for Moses, and one for E·liʹjah.” He did not realize what he was saying.

25439.label: Luke 9:34
25439.text: But as he was saying these things, a cloud formed and began to overshadow them. As they entered into the cloud, they became afraid.

25440.label: Luke 9:35
25440.text: Then a voice came out of the cloud, saying: “This is my Son, the one who has been chosen. Listen to him.”

25441.label: Luke 9:36
25441.text: As the voice spoke, Jesus was found alone. But they kept quiet and did not report to anyone in those days any of the things they saw.

25442.label: Luke 9:37
25442.text: The following day when they came down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.

25443.label: Luke 9:38
25443.text: And look! a man called out from the crowd, saying: “Teacher, I beg you to take a look at my son, because he is my only one.

25444.label: Luke 9:39
25444.text: And look! a spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it throws him into convulsions with foaming at the mouth, and only with difficulty does it leave him after bruising him.

25445.label: Luke 9:40
25445.text: I begged your disciples to expel it, but they could not.”

25446.label: Luke 9:41
25446.text: In response Jesus said: “O faithless and twisted generation, how long must I continue with you and put up with you? Bring your son over here.”

25447.label: Luke 9:42
25447.text: But even as he was approaching, the demon hurled him to the ground and violently threw him into a convulsion. However, Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy and gave him back to his father.

25448.label: Luke 9:43
25448.text: And they were all astounded at the majestic power of God. While they were all astonished at all the things he was doing, he said to his disciples:

25449.label: Luke 9:44
25449.text: “Listen carefully and remember these words, for the Son of man is going to be betrayed into men’s hands.”

25450.label: Luke 9:45
25450.text: But they did not understand what he was saying. In fact, it was concealed from them so that they might not grasp it, and they were afraid to question him about this saying.

25451.label: Luke 9:46
25451.text: Then a dispute arose among them about which one of them was the greatest.

25452.label: Luke 9:47
25452.text: Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their hearts, took a young child, stood him beside him,

25453.label: Luke 9:48
25453.text: and said to them: “Whoever receives this young child on the basis of my name receives me also; and whoever receives me also receives the One who sent me. For the one who conducts himself as a lesser one among all of you is the one who is great.”

25454.label: Luke 9:49
25454.text: In response John said: “Instructor, we saw someone expelling demons by using your name, and we tried to prevent him, because he is not following with us.”

25455.label: Luke 9:50
25455.text: But Jesus said to him: “Do not try to prevent him, for whoever is not against you is for you.”

25456.label: Luke 9:51
25456.text: As the days were drawing near for him to be taken up, he resolutely set his face to go to Jerusalem.

25457.label: Luke 9:52
25457.text: So he sent messengers ahead of him. And they went and entered a village of Sa·marʹi·tans to make preparations for him.

25458.label: Luke 9:53
25458.text: But they did not receive him, because he was determined to go to Jerusalem.

25459.label: Luke 9:54
25459.text: When the disciples James and John saw this, they said: “Lord, do you want us to call fire down from heaven and annihilate them?”

25460.label: Luke 9:55
25460.text: But he turned and rebuked them.

25461.label: Luke 9:56
25461.text: So they went to a different village.

25462.label: Luke 9:57
25462.text: Now as they were going along the road, someone said to him: “I will follow you wherever you go.”

25463.label: Luke 9:58
25463.text: But Jesus said to him: “Foxes have dens and birds of heaven have nests, but the Son of man has nowhere to lay down his head.”

25464.label: Luke 9:59
25464.text: Then he said to another: “Be my follower.” The man said: “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.”

25465.label: Luke 9:60
25465.text: But he said to him: “Let the dead bury their dead, but you go and declare abroad the Kingdom of God.”

25466.label: Luke 9:61
25466.text: And still another said: “I will follow you, Lord, but first permit me to say good-bye to those in my household.”

25467.label: Luke 9:62
25467.text: Jesus said to him: “No man who has put his hand to a plow and looks at the things behind is well-suited for the Kingdom of God.”

25468.label: Luke 10:1
25468.text: After these things the Lord designated 70 others and sent them out by twos ahead of him into every city and place where he himself was to go.

25469.label: Luke 10:2
25469.text: Then he said to them: “Yes, the harvest is great, but the workers are few. Therefore, beg the Master of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.

25470.label: Luke 10:3
25470.text: Go! Look! I am sending you out as lambs in among wolves.

25471.label: Luke 10:4
25471.text: Do not carry a money bag or a food pouch or sandals, and do not greet anyone along the road.

25472.label: Luke 10:5
25472.text: Wherever you enter into a house, say first: ‘May this house have peace.’

25473.label: Luke 10:6
25473.text: And if a friend of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him. But if there is not, it will return to you.

25474.label: Luke 10:7
25474.text: So stay in that house, eating and drinking the things they provide, for the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not keep transferring from house to house.

25475.label: Luke 10:8
25475.text: “Also, wherever you enter into a city and they receive you, eat what is set before you

25476.label: Luke 10:9
25476.text: and cure the sick ones in it and tell them: ‘The Kingdom of God has come near to you.’

25477.label: Luke 10:10
25477.text: But wherever you enter into a city and they do not receive you, go out into its main streets and say:

25478.label: Luke 10:11
25478.text: ‘We wipe off against you even the dust that sticks to our feet from your city. Nevertheless, know this, that the Kingdom of God has come near.’

25479.label: Luke 10:12
25479.text: I tell you that it will be more endurable for Sodʹom in that day than for that city.

25480.label: Luke 10:13
25480.text: “Woe to you, Cho·raʹzin! Woe to you, Beth·saʹi·da! because if the powerful works that have taken place in you had taken place in Tyre and Siʹdon, they would long ago have repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

25481.label: Luke 10:14
25481.text: Consequently, it will be more endurable for Tyre and Siʹdon in the judgment than for you.

25482.label: Luke 10:15
25482.text: And you, Ca·perʹna·um, will you perhaps be exalted to heaven? Down to the Grave you will come!

25483.label: Luke 10:16
25483.text: “Whoever listens to you listens to me. And whoever disregards you disregards me also. Moreover, whoever disregards me disregards also Him who sent me.”

25484.label: Luke 10:17
25484.text: Then the 70 returned with joy, saying: “Lord, even the demons are made subject to us by the use of your name.”

25485.label: Luke 10:18
25485.text: At that he said to them: “I see Satan already fallen like lightning from heaven.

25486.label: Luke 10:19
25486.text: Look! I have given you the authority to trample underfoot serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing at all will harm you.

25487.label: Luke 10:20
25487.text: Nevertheless, do not rejoice because the spirits are made subject to you, but rejoice because your names have been written in the heavens.”

25488.label: Luke 10:21
25488.text: In that very hour he became overjoyed in the holy spirit and said: “I publicly praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have carefully hidden these things from wise and intellectual ones and have revealed them to young children. Yes, O Father, because this is the way you approved.

25489.label: Luke 10:22
25489.text: All things have been handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son is willing to reveal him.”

25490.label: Luke 10:23
25490.text: With that he turned to the disciples and told them privately: “Happy are the eyes that see the things you are seeing.

25491.label: Luke 10:24
25491.text: For I say to you, many prophets and kings desired to see the things you are observing but did not see them, and to hear the things you are hearing but did not hear them.”

25492.label: Luke 10:25
25492.text: Now look! a man versed in the Law stood up to test him and said: “Teacher, what do I need to do to inherit everlasting life?”

25493.label: Luke 10:26
25493.text: He said to him: “What is written in the Law? How do you read?”

25494.label: Luke 10:27
25494.text: In answer he said: “‘You must love Jehovah your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole strength and with your whole mind’ and ‘your neighbor as yourself.’”

25495.label: Luke 10:28
25495.text: He said to him: “You answered correctly; keep doing this and you will get life.”

25496.label: Luke 10:29
25496.text: But wanting to prove himself righteous, the man said to Jesus: “Who really is my neighbor?”

25497.label: Luke 10:30
25497.text: In reply Jesus said: “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jerʹi·cho and fell victim to robbers, who stripped him, beat him, and went off, leaving him half-dead.

25498.label: Luke 10:31
25498.text: Now by coincidence a priest was going down on that road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the opposite side.

25499.label: Luke 10:32
25499.text: Likewise, a Levite, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the opposite side.

25500.label: Luke 10:33
25500.text: But a certain Sa·marʹi·tan traveling the road came upon him, and at seeing him, he was moved with pity.

25501.label: Luke 10:34
25501.text: So he approached him and bandaged his wounds, pouring oil and wine on them. Then he mounted him on his own animal and brought him to an inn and took care of him.

25502.label: Luke 10:35
25502.text: The next day he took out two de·narʹi·i, gave them to the innkeeper, and said: ‘Take care of him, and whatever you spend besides this, I will repay you when I return.’

25503.label: Luke 10:36
25503.text: Who of these three seems to you to have made himself neighbor to the man who fell victim to the robbers?”

25504.label: Luke 10:37
25504.text: He said: “The one who acted mercifully toward him.” Jesus then said to him: “Go and do the same yourself.”

25505.label: Luke 10:38
25505.text: Now as they went on their way, he entered into a certain village. Here a woman named Martha received him as a guest in her house.

25506.label: Luke 10:39
25506.text: She also had a sister called Mary, who sat down at the feet of the Lord and kept listening to what he was saying.

25507.label: Luke 10:40
