25507.text: Martha, on the other hand, was distracted with attending to many duties. So she came to him and said: “Lord, does it not matter to you that my sister has left me alone to attend to things? Tell her to come and help me.”

25508.label: Luke 10:41
25508.text: In answer the Lord said to her: “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and disturbed about many things.

25509.label: Luke 10:42
25509.text: A few things, though, are needed, or just one. For her part, Mary chose the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”

25510.label: Luke 11:1
25510.text: Now he was in a certain place praying, and when he stopped, one of his disciples said to him: “Lord, teach us how to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”

25511.label: Luke 11:2
25511.text: So he said to them: “Whenever you pray, say: ‘Father, let your name be sanctified. Let your Kingdom come.

25512.label: Luke 11:3
25512.text: Give us each day our bread according to our daily needs.

25513.label: Luke 11:4
25513.text: And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is in debt to us; and do not bring us into temptation.’”

25514.label: Luke 11:5
25514.text: Then he said to them: “Suppose one of you has a friend and you go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves,

25515.label: Luke 11:6
25515.text: because one of my friends has just come to me on a journey and I have nothing to offer him.’

25516.label: Luke 11:7
25516.text: But that one replies from inside: ‘Stop bothering me. The door is already locked, and my young children are with me in bed. I cannot get up and give you anything.’

25517.label: Luke 11:8
25517.text: I tell you, even if he will not get up and give him anything because of being his friend, certainly because of his bold persistence he will get up and give him whatever he needs.

25518.label: Luke 11:9
25518.text: So I say to you, keep on asking, and it will be given you; keep on seeking, and you will find; keep on knocking, and it will be opened to you.

25519.label: Luke 11:10
25519.text: For everyone asking receives, and everyone seeking finds, and to everyone knocking, it will be opened.

25520.label: Luke 11:11
25520.text: Indeed, which father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will hand him a serpent instead of a fish?

25521.label: Luke 11:12
25521.text: Or if he also asks for an egg, will hand him a scorpion?

25522.label: Luke 11:13
25522.text: Therefore, if you, although being wicked, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more so will the Father in heaven give holy spirit to those asking him!”

25523.label: Luke 11:14
25523.text: Later he expelled a speechless demon. After the demon came out, the speechless man spoke, and the crowds were amazed.

25524.label: Luke 11:15
25524.text: But some of them said: “He expels the demons by means of Be·elʹze·bub, the ruler of the demons.”

25525.label: Luke 11:16
25525.text: And others, to test him, began demanding a sign out of heaven from him.

25526.label: Luke 11:17
25526.text: Knowing their thinking, he said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself comes to ruin, and a house divided against itself falls.

25527.label: Luke 11:18
25527.text: In the same way, if Satan is also divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say I expel the demons by means of Be·elʹze·bub.

25528.label: Luke 11:19
25528.text: If I expel the demons by means of Be·elʹze·bub, by whom do your sons expel them? This is why they will be your judges.

25529.label: Luke 11:20
25529.text: But if it is by means of God’s finger that I expel the demons, the Kingdom of God has really overtaken you.

25530.label: Luke 11:21
25530.text: When a strong, well-armed man guards his palace, his belongings remain secure.

25531.label: Luke 11:22
25531.text: But when someone stronger than he is comes against him and conquers him, that man takes away all his weapons in which he was trusting, and he divides up the things he took from him.

25532.label: Luke 11:23
25532.text: Whoever is not on my side is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.

25533.label: Luke 11:24
25533.text: “When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through waterless places in search of a resting-place, and after finding none, it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I moved.’

25534.label: Luke 11:25
25534.text: And on arriving, it finds the house swept clean and adorned.

25535.label: Luke 11:26
25535.text: Then it goes and takes along seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and after getting inside, they dwell there. So the final circumstances of that man become worse than the first.”

25536.label: Luke 11:27
25536.text: Now as he was saying these things, a woman from the crowd called out to him: “Happy is the womb that carried you and the breasts that nursed you!”

25537.label: Luke 11:28
25537.text: But he said: “No, rather, happy are those hearing the word of God and keeping it!”

25538.label: Luke 11:29
25538.text: When the crowds were massing together, he began to say: “This generation is a wicked generation; it looks for a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Joʹnah.

25539.label: Luke 11:30
25539.text: For just as Joʹnah became a sign to the Ninʹe·vites, so will the Son of man be to this generation.

25540.label: Luke 11:31
25540.text: The queen of the south will be raised up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solʹo·mon. But look! something more than Solʹo·mon is here.

25541.label: Luke 11:32
25541.text: The men of Ninʹe·veh will rise in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because they repented at what Joʹnah preached. But look! something more than Joʹnah is here.

25542.label: Luke 11:33
25542.text: After lighting a lamp, a person puts it, not in a hidden place nor under a basket, but on the lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.

25543.label: Luke 11:34
25543.text: The lamp of the body is your eye. When your eye is focused, your whole body is also bright; but when it is envious, your body is also dark.

25544.label: Luke 11:35
25544.text: Be alert, therefore, that the light that is in you is not darkness.

25545.label: Luke 11:36
25545.text: Therefore, if your whole body is bright with no part of it dark, it will all be as bright as when a lamp gives you light by its rays.”

25546.label: Luke 11:37
25546.text: When he had said this, a Pharisee asked him to dine with him. So he went in and reclined at the table.

25547.label: Luke 11:38
25547.text: However, the Pharisee was surprised at seeing that he did not first wash before the dinner.

25548.label: Luke 11:39
25548.text: But the Lord said to him: “Now you Pharisees, you cleanse the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greediness and wickedness.

25549.label: Luke 11:40
25549.text: Unreasonable ones! The one who made the outside made also the inside, did he not?

25550.label: Luke 11:41
25550.text: But give as gifts of mercy the things that are from within, and look! everything about you will be clean.

25551.label: Luke 11:42
25551.text: But woe to you Pharisees, because you give the tenth of the mint and of the rue and of every other garden herb, but you disregard the justice and the love of God! These things you were under obligation to do, but not to disregard those other things.

25552.label: Luke 11:43
25552.text: Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the front seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces!

25553.label: Luke 11:44
25553.text: Woe to you, because you are as those graves that are not clearly visible, that men walk on and do not know it!”

25554.label: Luke 11:45
25554.text: In reply one of those versed in the Law said to him: “Teacher, in saying these things, you insult us also.”

25555.label: Luke 11:46
25555.text: Then he said: “Woe also to you who are versed in the Law, because you load men down with loads hard to carry, but you yourselves do not touch the loads with one of your fingers!

25556.label: Luke 11:47
25556.text: “Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, but your forefathers killed them!

25557.label: Luke 11:48
25557.text: Certainly you are witnesses of the deeds of your forefathers, and yet you approve of them, for they killed the prophets but you are building their tombs.

25558.label: Luke 11:49
25558.text: That is why the wisdom of God also said: ‘I will send prophets and apostles to them, and they will kill and persecute some of them,

25559.label: Luke 11:50
25559.text: so that the blood of all the prophets spilled from the founding of the world may be charged against this generation,

25560.label: Luke 11:51
25560.text: from the blood of Abel down to the blood of Zech·a·riʹah, who was killed between the altar and the house.’ Yes, I tell you, it will be charged against this generation.

25561.label: Luke 11:52
25561.text: “Woe to you who are versed in the Law, because you took away the key of knowledge. You yourselves did not go in, and you hinder those going in!”

25562.label: Luke 11:53
25562.text: So when he went out from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to put extreme pressure on him and to ply him with many more questions,

25563.label: Luke 11:54
25563.text: lying in wait for him to catch him in something he might say.

25564.label: Luke 12:1
25564.text: In the meantime, when a crowd of so many thousands had gathered together that they were stepping on one another, he started by saying first to his disciples: “Watch out for the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

25565.label: Luke 12:2
25565.text: But there is nothing carefully concealed that will not be revealed, and nothing secret that will not become known.

25566.label: Luke 12:3
25566.text: Therefore, whatever you say in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you whisper in private rooms will be preached from the housetops.

25567.label: Luke 12:4
25567.text: Moreover, I say to you, my friends, do not fear those who kill the body and after this are not able to do anything more.

25568.label: Luke 12:5
25568.text: But I will show you whom to fear: Fear the One who after killing has authority to throw into Ge·henʹna. Yes, I tell you, fear this One.

25569.label: Luke 12:6
25569.text: Five sparrows sell for two coins of small value, do they not? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.

25570.label: Luke 12:7
25570.text: But even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Have no fear; you are worth more than many sparrows.

25571.label: Luke 12:8
25571.text: “I say to you, everyone who acknowledges me before men, the Son of man will also acknowledge him before the angels of God.

25572.label: Luke 12:9
25572.text: But whoever disowns me before men will be disowned before the angels of God.

25573.label: Luke 12:10
25573.text: And everyone who says a word against the Son of man, it will be forgiven him, but whoever blasphemes against the holy spirit will not be forgiven.

25574.label: Luke 12:11
25574.text: When they bring you in before public assemblies, government officials, and authorities, do not become anxious about how or what you will speak in defense or what you will say,

25575.label: Luke 12:12
25575.text: for the holy spirit will teach you in that very hour the things you should say.”

25576.label: Luke 12:13
25576.text: Then someone in the crowd said to him: “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

25577.label: Luke 12:14
25577.text: He said to him: “Man, who appointed me judge or arbitrator between you two?”

25578.label: Luke 12:15
25578.text: Then he said to them: “Keep your eyes open and guard against every sort of greed, because even when a person has an abundance, his life does not result from the things he possesses.”

25579.label: Luke 12:16
25579.text: With that he told them an illustration, saying: “The land of a rich man produced well.

25580.label: Luke 12:17
25580.text: So he began reasoning within himself, ‘What should I do now that I have nowhere to gather my crops?’

25581.label: Luke 12:18
25581.text: Then he said, ‘I will do this: I will tear down my storehouses and build bigger ones, and there I will gather all my grain and all my goods,

25582.label: Luke 12:19
25582.text: and I will say to myself: “You have many good things stored up for many years; take it easy, eat, drink, enjoy yourself.”’

25583.label: Luke 12:20
25583.text: But God said to him, ‘Unreasonable one, this night they are demanding your life from you. Who, then, is to have the things you stored up?’

25584.label: Luke 12:21
25584.text: So it goes with the man who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”

25585.label: Luke 12:22
25585.text: Then he said to his disciples: “That is why I say to you, stop being anxious about your lives as to what you will eat or about your bodies as to what you will wear.

25586.label: Luke 12:23
25586.text: For the life is worth more than food and the body more than clothing.

25587.label: Luke 12:24
25587.text: Consider the ravens: They neither sow seed nor reap; they have neither barn nor storehouse; yet God feeds them. Are you not worth much more than birds?

25588.label: Luke 12:25
25588.text: Who of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his life span?

25589.label: Luke 12:26
25589.text: If, therefore, you cannot do such a small thing, why be anxious about the remaining things?

25590.label: Luke 12:27
25590.text: Consider how the lilies grow: They neither toil nor spin; but I tell you that not even Solʹo·mon in all his glory was arrayed as one of these.

25591.label: Luke 12:28
25591.text: Now if this is how God clothes the vegetation in the field that today exists and tomorrow is cast into an oven, how much more will he clothe you, you with little faith!

25592.label: Luke 12:29
25592.text: So stop seeking what you will eat and what you will drink, and stop being in anxious suspense;

25593.label: Luke 12:30
25593.text: for all these are the things the nations of the world are eagerly pursuing, but your Father knows you need these things.

25594.label: Luke 12:31
25594.text: Instead, keep seeking his Kingdom, and these things will be added to you.

25595.label: Luke 12:32
25595.text: “Have no fear, little flock, for your Father has approved of giving you the Kingdom.

25596.label: Luke 12:33
25596.text: Sell your belongings and give gifts of mercy. Make money pouches that do not wear out, a never-failing treasure in the heavens, where no thief gets near and no moth consumes.

25597.label: Luke 12:34
25597.text: For where your treasure is, there your hearts will be also.

25598.label: Luke 12:35
25598.text: “Be dressed and ready and have your lamps burning,

25599.label: Luke 12:36
25599.text: and you should be like men waiting for their master to return from the marriage, so when he comes and knocks, they may at once open to him.

25600.label: Luke 12:37
25600.text: Happy are those slaves whom the master on coming finds watching! Truly I say to you, he will dress himself for service and have them recline at the table and will come alongside and minister to them.

25601.label: Luke 12:38
25601.text: And if he comes in the second watch, even if in the third, and finds them ready, happy are they!

25602.label: Luke 12:39
25602.text: But know this, if the householder had known at what hour the thief would come, he would not have let his house be broken into.

25603.label: Luke 12:40
25603.text: You also, keep ready, because at an hour that you do not think likely, the Son of man is coming.”

25604.label: Luke 12:41
25604.text: Then Peter said: “Lord, are you telling this illustration just to us or also to everyone?”

25605.label: Luke 12:42
25605.text: And the Lord said: “Who really is the faithful steward, the discreet one, whom his master will appoint over his body of attendants to keep giving them their measure of food supplies at the proper time?

25606.label: Luke 12:43
25606.text: Happy is that slave if his master on coming finds him doing so!

25607.label: Luke 12:44
25607.text: I tell you truthfully, he will appoint him over all his belongings.

25608.label: Luke 12:45
25608.text: But if ever that slave should say in his heart, ‘My master delays coming,’ and starts to beat the male and female servants and to eat and drink and get drunk,

25609.label: Luke 12:46
25609.text: the master of that slave will come on a day that he is not expecting him and at an hour that he does not know, and he will punish him with the greatest severity and assign him a part with the unfaithful ones.

25610.label: Luke 12:47
25610.text: Then that slave who understood the will of his master but did not get ready or do what he asked will be beaten with many strokes.

25611.label: Luke 12:48
25611.text: But the one who did not understand and yet did things deserving of strokes will be beaten with few. Indeed, everyone to whom much was given, much will be demanded of him, and the one who was put in charge of much will have more than usual demanded of him.

25612.label: Luke 12:49
25612.text: “I came to start a fire on the earth, and what more is there for me to wish if it has already been lit?

25613.label: Luke 12:50
25613.text: Indeed, I have a baptism with which to be baptized, and how I am distressed until it is finished!

25614.label: Luke 12:51
25614.text: Do you think I came to give peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.

25615.label: Luke 12:52
25615.text: For from now on there will be five in one house divided, three against two and two against three.

25616.label: Luke 12:53
25616.text: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”

25617.label: Luke 12:54
25617.text: Then he also said to the crowds: “When you see a cloud rising in the west, at once you say, ‘A storm is coming,’ and it happens.

25618.label: Luke 12:55
25618.text: And when you see that a south wind is blowing, you say, ‘There will be a heat wave,’ and it occurs.

25619.label: Luke 12:56
25619.text: Hypocrites, you know how to examine the appearance of earth and sky, but why do you not know how to examine this particular time?

25620.label: Luke 12:57
25620.text: Why do you not judge also for yourselves what is righteous?

25621.label: Luke 12:58
25621.text: For example, when you are going with your legal opponent to a ruler, while on the way, get to work to settle the dispute with him so that he may not summon you before the judge, and the judge deliver you to the court officer, and the court officer throw you into prison.

25622.label: Luke 12:59
25622.text: I tell you, you will certainly not get out of there until you pay over your last small coin.”

25623.label: Luke 13:1
25623.text: At that time some who were present reported to him about the Gal·i·leʹans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

25624.label: Luke 13:2
25624.text: In reply he said to them: “Do you think that those Gal·i·leʹans were worse sinners than all other Gal·i·leʹans because they have suffered these things?

25625.label: Luke 13:3
25625.text: No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise be destroyed.

25626.label: Luke 13:4
25626.text: Or those 18 on whom the tower in Si·loʹam fell, killing them—do you think that they had greater guilt than all other men who live in Jerusalem?

25627.label: Luke 13:5
25627.text: No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all be destroyed, as they were.”

25628.label: Luke 13:6
25628.text: Then he went on to tell this illustration: “A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it but found none.

25629.label: Luke 13:7
25629.text: Then he said to the vinedresser, ‘Here it is three years that I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, but have found none. Cut it down! Why should it keep the ground useless?’

25630.label: Luke 13:8
25630.text: In reply he said to him, ‘Master, leave it alone for one more year until I dig around it and put on manure.

25631.label: Luke 13:9
25631.text: If it produces fruit in the future, well and good; but if not, then cut it down.’”

25632.label: Luke 13:10
25632.text: Now he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.

25633.label: Luke 13:11
25633.text: And look! a woman was there who had had a spirit of weakness for 18 years; and she was bent double and was unable to straighten up at all.

25634.label: Luke 13:12
25634.text: When he saw her, Jesus addressed her and said: “Woman, you are released from your weakness.”

25635.label: Luke 13:13
25635.text: And he laid his hands on her, and instantly she straightened up and began to glorify God.

25636.label: Luke 13:14
25636.text: But in response the presiding officer of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus did the cure on the Sabbath, said to the crowd: “There are six days on which work ought to be done; so come and be cured on those days, and not on the Sabbath day.”

25637.label: Luke 13:15
25637.text: However, the Lord answered him: “Hypocrites, does not each one of you on the Sabbath untie his bull or his donkey from the stall and lead it away to give it something to drink?

25638.label: Luke 13:16
25638.text: Should not this woman, who is a daughter of Abraham and whom Satan held bound for 18 years, be released from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”

25639.label: Luke 13:17
25639.text: Well, when he said these things, all his opposers began to feel shame, but the entire crowd began to rejoice at all the glorious things he did.

25640.label: Luke 13:18
25640.text: So he went on to say: “What is the Kingdom of God like, and with what can I compare it?

25641.label: Luke 13:19
25641.text: It is like a mustard grain that a man took and planted in his garden, and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of heaven nested in its branches.”

25642.label: Luke 13:20
25642.text: And again he said: “With what can I compare the Kingdom of God?

25643.label: Luke 13:21
25643.text: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed with three large measures of flour until the whole mass was fermented.”

25644.label: Luke 13:22
25644.text: And he traveled from city to city and from village to village, teaching and continuing on his journey to Jerusalem.

25645.label: Luke 13:23
25645.text: Now a man said to him: “Lord, are those being saved few?” He said to them:

25646.label: Luke 13:24
25646.text: “Exert yourselves vigorously to get in through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will seek to get in but will not be able.

25647.label: Luke 13:25
25647.text: When the householder gets up and locks the door, you will stand outside knocking at the door, saying, ‘Lord, open to us.’ But in answer he will say to you: ‘I do not know where you are from.’

25648.label: Luke 13:26
25648.text: Then you will start saying, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our main streets.’

25649.label: Luke 13:27
25649.text: But he will say to you, ‘I do not know where you are from. Get away from me, all you workers of unrighteousness!’

25650.label: Luke 13:28
25650.text: There is where your weeping and the gnashing of your teeth will be, when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the Kingdom of God, but you yourselves thrown outside.

25651.label: Luke 13:29
25651.text: Furthermore, people will come from east and west and from north and south, and will recline at the table in the Kingdom of God.

25652.label: Luke 13:30
25652.text: And look! there are those last who will be first, and there are those first who will be last.”

25653.label: Luke 13:31
25653.text: In that very hour some of the Pharisees came up and told him: “Get out and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill you.”

25654.label: Luke 13:32
25654.text: And he said to them: “Go and tell that fox, ‘Look! I am casting out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will be finished.’

25655.label: Luke 13:33
25655.text: Nevertheless, I must go on today, tomorrow, and the following day, because it cannot be that a prophet should be put to death outside of Jerusalem.

25656.label: Luke 13:34
25656.text: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the killer of the prophets and stoner of those sent to her —how often I wanted to gather your children together the way a hen gathers her brood of chicks under her wings! But you did not want it.

25657.label: Luke 13:35
25657.text: Look! Your house is abandoned to you. I tell you, you will by no means see me until you say: ‘Blessed is the one who comes in Jehovah’s name!’”

25658.label: Luke 14:1
25658.text: On another occasion he went to eat a meal in the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees on the Sabbath, and they were closely watching him.

25659.label: Luke 14:2
25659.text: And look! a man who had dropsy was in front of him.

25660.label: Luke 14:3
25660.text: So in response Jesus asked those versed in the Law and the Pharisees: “Is it lawful to cure on the Sabbath or not?”

25661.label: Luke 14:4
25661.text: But they kept silent. With that he took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him away.

25662.label: Luke 14:5
25662.text: Then he said to them: “Who of you, if his son or bull falls into a well, will not immediately pull him out on the Sabbath day?”

25663.label: Luke 14:6
25663.text: And they were not able to reply to this.

25664.label: Luke 14:7
25664.text: He then told the invited men an illustration when he noticed how they were choosing the most prominent places for themselves. He said to them:

25665.label: Luke 14:8
25665.text: “When you are invited by someone to a marriage feast, do not recline in the most prominent place. Perhaps someone more distinguished than you may also have been invited.

25666.label: Luke 14:9
25666.text: Then the one who invited you both will come and say to you, ‘Let this man have your place.’ Then you will proceed with shame to take the lowest place.

25667.label: Luke 14:10
25667.text: But when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, so that when the man who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, go on up higher.’ Then you will have honor in front of all your fellow guests.

25668.label: Luke 14:11
25668.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

25669.label: Luke 14:12
25669.text: Next he said also to the man who had invited him: “When you spread a dinner or an evening meal, do not call your friends or your brothers or your relatives or your rich neighbors. Otherwise, they might also invite you in return, and it would become a repayment to you.

25670.label: Luke 14:13
25670.text: But when you spread a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind;

25671.label: Luke 14:14
25671.text: and you will be happy, because they have nothing with which to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous ones.”

25672.label: Luke 14:15
25672.text: On hearing these things, one of the fellow guests said to him: “Happy is the one who dines in the Kingdom of God.”

25673.label: Luke 14:16
25673.text: Jesus said to him: “A man was spreading a grand evening meal, and he invited many.

25674.label: Luke 14:17
25674.text: He sent his slave out at the hour of the evening meal to say to the invited ones, ‘Come, because everything is now ready.’

25675.label: Luke 14:18
25675.text: But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said to him, ‘I bought a field and need to go out and see it; I ask you, have me excused.’

25676.label: Luke 14:19
25676.text: And another said, ‘I bought five yoke of cattle and am going to examine them; I ask you, have me excused.’

25677.label: Luke 14:20
25677.text: Still another said, ‘I just got married, and for this reason I cannot come.’

25678.label: Luke 14:21
25678.text: So the slave came and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his slave, ‘Go out quickly to the main streets and the alleys of the city, and bring in here the poor and crippled and blind and lame.’

25679.label: Luke 14:22
25679.text: In time the slave said, ‘Master, what you ordered has been done, and still there is room.’

25680.label: Luke 14:23
25680.text: So the master said to the slave, ‘Go out to the roads and the lanes and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.

25681.label: Luke 14:24
25681.text: For I say to you, none of those men who were invited will taste my evening meal.’”

25682.label: Luke 14:25
25682.text: Now large crowds were traveling with him, and he turned and said to them:

25683.label: Luke 14:26
25683.text: “If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple.

25684.label: Luke 14:27
25684.text: Whoever does not carry his torture stake and come after me cannot be my disciple.

25685.label: Luke 14:28
25685.text: For example, who of you wanting to build a tower does not first sit down and calculate the expense to see if he has enough to complete it?

25686.label: Luke 14:29
25686.text: Otherwise, he might lay its foundation but not be able to finish it, and all the onlookers would start to ridicule him,

25687.label: Luke 14:30
25687.text: saying: ‘This man started to build but was not able to finish.’

25688.label: Luke 14:31
25688.text: Or what king marching out against another king in war does not first sit down and take counsel whether he is able with 10,000 troops to stand up to the one who comes against him with 20,000?

25689.label: Luke 14:32
25689.text: If, in fact, he cannot do so, then while that one is yet far away, he sends out a body of ambassadors and sues for peace.

25690.label: Luke 14:33
25690.text: In the same way, you may be sure that not one of you who does not say good-bye to all his belongings can be my disciple.

25691.label: Luke 14:34
25691.text: “Salt, to be sure, is fine. But if the salt loses its strength, with what will it be seasoned?

25692.label: Luke 14:35
25692.text: It is not suitable for soil or for manure. People throw it away. Let the one who has ears to listen, listen.”

25693.label: Luke 15:1
25693.text: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners kept gathering around him to hear him.

25694.label: Luke 15:2
25694.text: And both the Pharisees and the scribes kept muttering: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”

25695.label: Luke 15:3
25695.text: Then he told them this illustration, saying:

25696.label: Luke 15:4
25696.text: “What man among you with 100 sheep, on losing one of them, will not leave the 99 behind in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?

25697.label: Luke 15:5
25697.text: And when he has found it, he puts it on his shoulders and rejoices.

25698.label: Luke 15:6
25698.text: And when he gets home, he calls his friends and his neighbors together, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.’

25699.label: Luke 15:7
25699.text: I tell you that in the same way, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over 99 righteous ones who have no need of repentance.

25700.label: Luke 15:8
25700.text: “Or what woman who has ten drachma coins, if she loses one of the drachmas, does not light a lamp and sweep her house and search carefully until she finds it?

25701.label: Luke 15:9
25701.text: And when she has found it, she calls her friends and neighbors together, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma coin that I had lost.’

25702.label: Luke 15:10
25702.text: In the same way, I tell you, joy arises among the angels of God over one sinner who repents.”

25703.label: Luke 15:11
25703.text: Then he said: “A man had two sons.

25704.label: Luke 15:12
25704.text: And the younger one said to his father, ‘Father, give me the share of the property that should come to me.’ So he divided his belongings between them.

25705.label: Luke 15:13
25705.text: A few days later, the younger son gathered all his things together and traveled to a distant country and there squandered his property by living a debauched life.

25706.label: Luke 15:14
25706.text: When he had spent everything, a severe famine occurred throughout that country, and he fell into need.

25707.label: Luke 15:15
25707.text: He even went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, who sent him into his fields to herd swine.

25708.label: Luke 15:16
25708.text: And he longed to be filled with the carob pods that the swine were eating, but no one would give him anything.

25709.label: Luke 15:17
25709.text: “When he came to his senses, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired men have more than enough bread, while I am dying here from hunger!

25710.label: Luke 15:18
25710.text: I will get up and travel to my father and say to him: “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.

25711.label: Luke 15:19
25711.text: I am no longer worthy of being called your son. Make me as one of your hired men.”’

25712.label: Luke 15:20
25712.text: So he got up and went to his father. While he was still a long way off, his father caught sight of him and was moved with pity, and he ran and embraced him and tenderly kissed him.

25713.label: Luke 15:21
25713.text: Then the son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy of being called your son.’

25714.label: Luke 15:22
25714.text: But the father said to his slaves, ‘Quick! bring out a robe, the best one, and clothe him with it, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.

25715.label: Luke 15:23
25715.text: Also bring the fattened calf, slaughter it, and let us eat and celebrate,

25716.label: Luke 15:24
25716.text: for this son of mine was dead but has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.’ And they started to enjoy themselves.

25717.label: Luke 15:25
25717.text: “Now his older son was in the field, and as he returned and got near the house, he heard music and dancing.

25718.label: Luke 15:26
25718.text: So he called one of the servants to him and asked what was happening.

25719.label: Luke 15:27
25719.text: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father slaughtered the fattened calf because he got him back in good health.’

25720.label: Luke 15:28
25720.text: But he became angry and refused to go in. Then his father came out and began to plead with him.

25721.label: Luke 15:29
25721.text: In reply he said to his father, ‘Look! These many years I have slaved for you and never once did I disobey your orders, and yet you never once gave me a young goat to enjoy with my friends.

25722.label: Luke 15:30
25722.text: But as soon as this son of yours arrived who squandered your belongings with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him.’

25723.label: Luke 15:31
25723.text: Then he said to him, ‘My son, you have always been with me, and all the things that are mine are yours.

25724.label: Luke 15:32
25724.text: But we just had to celebrate and rejoice, for your brother was dead but has come to life; he was lost and has been found.’”

25725.label: Luke 16:1
25725.text: Then he also said to the disciples: “A rich man had a steward who was accused of handling his goods wastefully.

25726.label: Luke 16:2
25726.text: So he called him and said, ‘What is this I hear about you? Hand in the account of your stewardship, for you can no longer manage the house.’

25727.label: Luke 16:3
25727.text: Then the steward said to himself, ‘What am I to do, seeing that my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig, and I am ashamed to beg.

25728.label: Luke 16:4
25728.text: Ah! I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, people will welcome me into their homes.’

25729.label: Luke 16:5
25729.text: And calling to him each one of his master’s debtors, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’

25730.label: Luke 16:6
25730.text: He replied, ‘A hundred measures of olive oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take back your written agreement and sit down and quickly write 50.’

25731.label: Luke 16:7
25731.text: Next, he said to another one, ‘Now you, how much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred large measures of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take back your written agreement and write 80.’

25732.label: Luke 16:8
25732.text: And his master commended the steward, though unrighteous, because he acted with practical wisdom; for the sons of this system of things are wiser in a practical way toward their own generation than the sons of the light are.

25733.label: Luke 16:9
25733.text: “Also, I say to you: Make friends for yourselves by means of the unrighteous riches, so that when such fail, they may receive you into the everlasting dwelling places.

25734.label: Luke 16:10
25734.text: The person faithful in what is least is faithful also in much, and the person unrighteous in what is least is unrighteous also in much.

25735.label: Luke 16:11
25735.text: Therefore, if you have not proved yourselves faithful in connection with the unrighteous riches, who will entrust you with what is true?

25736.label: Luke 16:12
25736.text: And if you have not proved yourselves faithful in connection with what belongs to another, who will give you something for yourselves?

25737.label: Luke 16:13
25737.text: No servant can be a slave to two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will stick to the one and despise the other. You cannot be slaves to God and to Riches.”

25738.label: Luke 16:14
25738.text: Now the Pharisees, who were money lovers, were listening to all these things, and they began to sneer at him.

25739.label: Luke 16:15
25739.text: So he said to them: “You are those who declare yourselves righteous before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is considered exalted by men is a disgusting thing in God’s sight.

25740.label: Luke 16:16
25740.text: “The Law and the Prophets were until John. From then on, the Kingdom of God is being declared as good news, and every sort of person is pressing forward toward it.

25741.label: Luke 16:17
25741.text: Indeed, it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of a letter of the Law to go unfulfilled.

25742.label: Luke 16:18
25742.text: “Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and whoever marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.

25743.label: Luke 16:19
25743.text: “There was a rich man who used to dress in purple and linen, enjoying himself day after day with magnificence.

25744.label: Luke 16:20
25744.text: But a beggar named Lazʹa·rus used to be put at his gate, covered with ulcers

25745.label: Luke 16:21
25745.text: and desiring to be filled with the things dropping from the table of the rich man. Yes, even the dogs would come and lick his ulcers.

25746.label: Luke 16:22
25746.text: Now in the course of time, the beggar died and was carried off by the angels to Abraham’s side. “Also, the rich man died and was buried.

25747.label: Luke 16:23
25747.text: And in the Grave he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and he saw Abraham from afar and Lazʹa·rus by his side.

25748.label: Luke 16:24
25748.text: So he called and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazʹa·rus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in anguish in this blazing fire.’

25749.label: Luke 16:25
25749.text: But Abraham said, ‘Child, remember that you had your fill of good things in your lifetime, but Lazʹa·rus for his part received bad things. Now, however, he is being comforted here, but you are in anguish.

25750.label: Luke 16:26
25750.text: And besides all these things, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who want to go over from here to you cannot, neither may people cross over from there to us.’

25751.label: Luke 16:27
25751.text: Then he said, ‘That being so, I ask you, father, to send him to the house of my father,

25752.label: Luke 16:28
25752.text: for I have five brothers, in order that he may give them a thorough witness so that they will not also come into this place of torment.’

25753.label: Luke 16:29
25753.text: But Abraham said, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to these.’

25754.label: Luke 16:30
25754.text: Then he said, ‘No, indeed, father Abraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent.’

25755.label: Luke 16:31
25755.text: But he said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.’”

25756.label: Luke 17:1
25756.text: Then he said to his disciples: “It is unavoidable that causes for stumbling should come. Nevertheless, woe to the one through whom they come!

25757.label: Luke 17:2
25757.text: It would be more advantageous for him if a millstone were hung from his neck and he were thrown into the sea than for him to stumble one of these little ones.

25758.label: Luke 17:3
25758.text: Pay attention to yourselves. If your brother commits a sin, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.

25759.label: Luke 17:4
25759.text: Even if he sins seven times a day against you and he comes back to you seven times, saying, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”

25760.label: Luke 17:5
25760.text: Now the apostles said to the Lord: “Give us more faith.”

25761.label: Luke 17:6
25761.text: Then the Lord said: “If you had faith the size of a mustard grain, you would say to this black mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea!’ and it would obey you.

25762.label: Luke 17:7
25762.text: “Which one of you who has a slave plowing or shepherding would say to him when he comes in from the field, ‘Come here at once and dine at the table’?

25763.label: Luke 17:8
25763.text: Rather, will he not say to him, ‘Get something ready for me to have my evening meal, and put on an apron and serve me until I finish eating and drinking, and afterward you can eat and drink’?

25764.label: Luke 17:9
25764.text: He will not feel gratitude to the slave because he did what was assigned, will he?

25765.label: Luke 17:10
25765.text: Likewise, when you have done all the things assigned to you, say: ‘We are good-for-nothing slaves. What we have done is what we ought to have done.’”

25766.label: Luke 17:11
25766.text: While he was going to Jerusalem, he was passing between Sa·marʹi·a and Galʹi·lee.

25767.label: Luke 17:12
25767.text: And as he was entering a village, ten men with leprosy met him, but they stood at a distance.

25768.label: Luke 17:13
25768.text: And they raised their voices and said: “Jesus, Instructor, have mercy on us!”

25769.label: Luke 17:14
25769.text: When he saw them, he said to them: “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” Then as they were going off, they were cleansed.

25770.label: Luke 17:15
25770.text: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.

25771.label: Luke 17:16
25771.text: And he fell facedown at Jesus’ feet, thanking him. Furthermore, he was a Sa·marʹi·tan.

25772.label: Luke 17:17
25772.text: In reply Jesus said: “All ten were cleansed, were they not? Where, then, are the other nine?

25773.label: Luke 17:18
25773.text: Did no one else turn back to give glory to God except this man of another nation?”

25774.label: Luke 17:19
25774.text: Then he said to him: “Get up and be on your way; your faith has made you well.”

25775.label: Luke 17:20
25775.text: On being asked by the Pharisees when the Kingdom of God was coming, he answered them: “The Kingdom of God is not coming with striking observableness;

25776.label: Luke 17:21
25776.text: nor will people say, ‘See here!’ or, ‘There!’ For look! the Kingdom of God is in your midst.”

25777.label: Luke 17:22
25777.text: Then he said to the disciples: “Days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, but you will not see it.

25778.label: Luke 17:23
25778.text: And people will say to you, ‘See there!’ or, ‘See here!’ Do not go out or chase after them.

25779.label: Luke 17:24
25779.text: For just as lightning flashes from one part of heaven to another part of heaven, so the Son of man will be in his day.

25780.label: Luke 17:25
25780.text: First, however, he must undergo many sufferings and be rejected by this generation.

25781.label: Luke 17:26
25781.text: Moreover, just as it occurred in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of man:

25782.label: Luke 17:27
25782.text: they were eating, they were drinking, men were marrying, women were being given in marriage until that day when Noah entered into the ark, and the Flood came and destroyed them all.

25783.label: Luke 17:28
25783.text: Likewise, just as it occurred in the days of Lot: they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building.

25784.label: Luke 17:29
25784.text: But on the day that Lot went out of Sodʹom, it rained fire and sulfur from heaven and destroyed them all.

25785.label: Luke 17:30
25785.text: It will be the same on that day when the Son of man is revealed.

25786.label: Luke 17:31
25786.text: “On that day let the person who is on the housetop but whose belongings are in the house not come down to pick these up, and likewise, the person out in the field must not return to the things behind.

25788.label: Luke 17:33
25788.text: Whoever seeks to keep his life safe will lose it, but whoever loses it will preserve it alive.

25789.label: Luke 17:34
25789.text: I tell you, in that night two people will be in one bed; the one will be taken along, but the other will be abandoned.

25790.label: Luke 17:35
25790.text: There will be two women grinding at the same mill; the one will be taken along, but the other will be abandoned.”

25792.label: Luke 17:37
25792.text: So in response they said to him: “Where, Lord?” He said to them: “Where the body is, there also the eagles will be gathered together.”

25793.label: Luke 18:1
25793.text: Then he went on to tell them an illustration about the need for them always to pray and not to give up,

25794.label: Luke 18:2
25794.text: saying: “In a certain city there was a judge who had no fear of God and no respect for man.

25795.label: Luke 18:3
25795.text: There was also a widow in that city who kept going to him and saying, ‘See that I get justice from my legal opponent.’

25796.label: Luke 18:4
25796.text: Well, for a while he was unwilling, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Although I do not fear God or respect any man,

25797.label: Luke 18:5
25797.text: because this widow keeps making me trouble, I will see that she gets justice so that she will not keep coming and wearing me out with her demand.’”

25798.label: Luke 18:6
25798.text: Then the Lord said: “Hear what the judge, although unrighteous, said!

25799.label: Luke 18:7
25799.text: Certainly, then, will not God cause justice to be done for his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night, while he is patient toward them?

25800.label: Luke 18:8
25800.text: I tell you, he will cause justice to be done to them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of man arrives, will he really find this faith on the earth?”

25801.label: Luke 18:9
25801.text: He also told this illustration to some who trusted in their own righteousness and who considered others as nothing:

25802.label: Luke 18:10
25802.text: “Two men went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

25803.label: Luke 18:11
25803.text: The Pharisee stood and began to pray these things to himself, ‘O God, I thank you that I am not like everyone else—extortioners, unrighteous, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.

25804.label: Luke 18:12
25804.text: I fast twice a week; I give the tenth of all things I acquire.’

25805.label: Luke 18:13
25805.text: But the tax collector, standing at a distance, was not willing even to raise his eyes heavenward but kept beating his chest, saying, ‘O God, be gracious to me, a sinner.’

25806.label: Luke 18:14
25806.text: I tell you, this man went down to his home and was proved more righteous than that Pharisee. Because everyone who exalts himself will be humiliated, but whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

25807.label: Luke 18:15
25807.text: Now people were also bringing him their infants for him to touch them, but on seeing this, the disciples began to reprimand them.

25808.label: Luke 18:16
25808.text: However, Jesus called the infants to him, saying: “Let the young children come to me, and do not try to stop them, for the Kingdom of God belongs to such ones.

25809.label: Luke 18:17
25809.text: Truly I say to you, whoever does not receive the Kingdom of God like a young child will by no means enter into it.”

25810.label: Luke 18:18
25810.text: And one of the rulers questioned him, saying: “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit everlasting life?”

25811.label: Luke 18:19
25811.text: Jesus said to him: “Why do you call me good? Nobody is good except one, God.

25812.label: Luke 18:20
25812.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and your mother.’”

25813.label: Luke 18:21
25813.text: Then he said: “All of these I have kept from youth on.”

25814.label: Luke 18:22
25814.text: After hearing that, Jesus said to him, “There is still one thing lacking about you: Sell all the things you have and distribute the proceeds to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come be my follower.”

25815.label: Luke 18:23
25815.text: When he heard this, he became deeply grieved, for he was very rich.

25816.label: Luke 18:24
25816.text: Jesus looked at him and said: “How difficult it will be for those having money to make their way into the Kingdom of God!

25817.label: Luke 18:25
25817.text: It is easier, in fact, for a camel to get through the eye of a sewing needle than for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of God.”

25818.label: Luke 18:26
25818.text: Those who heard this said: “Who possibly can be saved?”

25819.label: Luke 18:27
25819.text: He said: “The things impossible with men are possible with God.”

25820.label: Luke 18:28
25820.text: But Peter said: “Look! We have left what was ours and followed you.”

25821.label: Luke 18:29
25821.text: He said to them: “Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the Kingdom of God

25822.label: Luke 18:30
25822.text: who will not get many times more in this period of time, and in the coming system of things, everlasting life.”

25823.label: Luke 18:31
25823.text: Then he took the Twelve aside and said to them: “Look! We are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things written by means of the prophets about the Son of man will be accomplished.

25824.label: Luke 18:32
25824.text: For instance, he will be handed over to men of the nations and will be mocked and treated insolently and spat on.

25825.label: Luke 18:33
25825.text: And after scourging him, they will kill him, but on the third day he will rise.”

25826.label: Luke 18:34
25826.text: However, they did not get the meaning of any of these things, for these words were hidden from them, and they did not understand the things said.

25827.label: Luke 18:35
25827.text: Now as Jesus was getting near to Jerʹi·cho, a blind man was sitting beside the road begging.

25828.label: Luke 18:36
25828.text: Because he heard a crowd passing by, he began to inquire what was going on.

25829.label: Luke 18:37
25829.text: They reported to him: “Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ is passing by!”

25830.label: Luke 18:38
25830.text: At that he cried out: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

25831.label: Luke 18:39
25831.text: And those who were in front began rebuking him, telling him to keep quiet, but all the more he kept shouting: “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

25832.label: Luke 18:40
25832.text: Then Jesus stopped and commanded that the man be brought to him. After he came near, Jesus asked him:

25833.label: Luke 18:41
25833.text: “What do you want me to do for you?” He said: “Lord, let me recover my sight.”

25834.label: Luke 18:42
25834.text: So Jesus said to him: “Recover your sight; your faith has made you well.”

25835.label: Luke 18:43
25835.text: And instantly he recovered his sight, and he began to follow him, glorifying God. Also, at seeing it, all the people gave praise to God.

25836.label: Luke 19:1
25836.text: He then entered Jerʹi·cho and was passing through.

25837.label: Luke 19:2
25837.text: Now a man named Zac·chaeʹus was there; he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.

25838.label: Luke 19:3
25838.text: Well, he was trying to see who this Jesus was, but he could not see because of the crowd, since he was short.

25839.label: Luke 19:4
25839.text: So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree in order to see him, for he was about to pass that way.

25840.label: Luke 19:5
25840.text: Now when Jesus got to the place, he looked up and said to him: “Zac·chaeʹus, hurry and get down, for today I must stay in your house.”

25841.label: Luke 19:6
25841.text: With that he hurried down and joyfully welcomed him as a guest.

25842.label: Luke 19:7
25842.text: When they saw this, they were all muttering: “He went as a guest to the house of a man who is a sinner.”

25843.label: Luke 19:8
25843.text: But Zac·chaeʹus stood up and said to the Lord: “Look! The half of my belongings, Lord, I am giving to the poor, and whatever I extorted from anyone, I am restoring four times over.”

25844.label: Luke 19:9
25844.text: At this Jesus said to him: “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.

25845.label: Luke 19:10
25845.text: For the Son of man came to seek and to save what was lost.”

25846.label: Luke 19:11
25846.text: While they were listening to these things, he told another illustration, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought that the Kingdom of God was going to appear instantly.

25847.label: Luke 19:12
25847.text: So he said: “A man of noble birth traveled to a distant land to secure kingly power for himself and to return.

25848.label: Luke 19:13
25848.text: Calling ten of his slaves, he gave them ten miʹnas and told them, ‘Do business with these until I come.’

25849.label: Luke 19:14
25849.text: But his citizens hated him and sent out a body of ambassadors after him to say, ‘We do not want this man to become king over us.’

25850.label: Luke 19:15
25850.text: “When he eventually got back after having secured the kingly power, he summoned the slaves to whom he had given the money, in order to ascertain what they had gained by their business activity.

25851.label: Luke 19:16
25851.text: So the first one came forward and said, ‘Lord, your miʹna gained ten miʹnas.’

25852.label: Luke 19:17
25852.text: He said to him, ‘Well done, good slave! Because in a very small matter you have proved yourself faithful, hold authority over ten cities.’

25853.label: Luke 19:18
25853.text: Now the second came, saying, ‘Your miʹna, Lord, made five miʹnas.’

25854.label: Luke 19:19
25854.text: He said to this one as well, ‘You too be in charge of five cities.’

25855.label: Luke 19:20
25855.text: But another one came, saying, ‘Lord, here is your miʹna that I kept hidden away in a cloth.

25856.label: Luke 19:21
25856.text: You see, I was in fear of you, because you are a harsh man; you take what you did not deposit, and you reap what you did not sow.’

25857.label: Luke 19:22
25857.text: He said to him, ‘By your own words I judge you, wicked slave. You knew, did you, that I am a harsh man, taking what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?

25858.label: Luke 19:23
25858.text: So why did you not put my money in a bank? Then on my coming, I would have collected it with interest.’

25859.label: Luke 19:24
25859.text: “With that he said to those standing by, ‘Take the miʹna from him and give it to the one who has the ten miʹnas.’

25860.label: Luke 19:25
25860.text: But they said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten miʹnas!’—

25861.label: Luke 19:26
25861.text: ‘I say to you, to everyone who has, more will be given, but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.

25862.label: Luke 19:27
25862.text: Moreover, bring these enemies of mine here who did not want me to become king over them and execute them in front of me.’”

25863.label: Luke 19:28
25863.text: After he had said these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.

25864.label: Luke 19:29
25864.text: And when he got near to Bethʹpha·ge and Bethʹa·ny at the mountain called Mount of Olives, he sent two of the disciples,

25865.label: Luke 19:30
25865.text: saying: “Go into the village that is within sight, and after you enter it, you will find a colt tied, on which no man has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.

25866.label: Luke 19:31
25866.text: But if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ you must say, ‘The Lord needs it.’”

25867.label: Luke 19:32
25867.text: So those who were sent went away and found it just as he had said to them.

25868.label: Luke 19:33
25868.text: But as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them: “Why are you untying the colt?”

25870.label: Luke 19:35
25870.text: And they led it to Jesus, and they threw their outer garments on the colt and seated Jesus on it.

25871.label: Luke 19:36
25871.text: As he moved along, they were spreading their outer garments on the road.

25872.label: Luke 19:37
25872.text: As soon as he got near the road down the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and to praise God with a loud voice because of all the powerful works they had seen,

25873.label: Luke 19:38
25873.text: saying: “Blessed is the one coming as the King in Jehovah’s name! Peace in heaven, and glory in the heights above!”

25874.label: Luke 19:39
25874.text: However, some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him: “Teacher, rebuke your disciples.”

25875.label: Luke 19:40
25875.text: But in reply he said: “I tell you, if these remained silent, the stones would cry out.”

25876.label: Luke 19:41
25876.text: And when he got nearby, he viewed the city and wept over it,

25877.label: Luke 19:42
25877.text: saying: “If you, even you, had discerned on this day the things having to do with peace —but now they have been hidden from your eyes.

25878.label: Luke 19:43
25878.text: Because the days will come upon you when your enemies will build around you a fortification of pointed stakes and will encircle you and besiege you from every side.

25879.label: Luke 19:44
25879.text: They will dash you and your children within you to the ground, and they will not leave a stone upon a stone in you, because you did not discern the time of your being inspected.”

25880.label: Luke 19:45
25880.text: Then he entered the temple and started to throw out those who were selling,

25881.label: Luke 19:46
25881.text: saying to them: “It is written, ‘My house will be a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a cave of robbers.”

25882.label: Luke 19:47
25882.text: He continued teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the principal ones of the people were seeking to kill him;

25883.label: Luke 19:48
25883.text: but they did not find any way to do this, for the people one and all kept hanging on to him to hear him.

25884.label: Luke 20:1
25884.text: On one of the days while he was teaching the people in the temple and declaring the good news, the chief priests and the scribes with the elders came

25885.label: Luke 20:2
25885.text: and said to him: “Tell us, by what authority do you do these things? Or who gave you this authority?”

25886.label: Luke 20:3
25886.text: He replied to them: “I will also ask you a question, and you tell me:

25887.label: Luke 20:4
25887.text: Was the baptism of John from heaven or from men?”

25888.label: Luke 20:5
25888.text: Then they drew conclusions among themselves, saying: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why did you not believe him?’

25889.label: Luke 20:6
25889.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ the people one and all will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”

25890.label: Luke 20:7
25890.text: So they replied that they did not know its source.

25891.label: Luke 20:8
25891.text: Jesus said to them: “Neither am I telling you by what authority I do these things.”

25892.label: Luke 20:9
25892.text: Then he began to tell the people this illustration: “A man planted a vineyard and leased it to cultivators, and he traveled abroad for a considerable time.

25893.label: Luke 20:10
25893.text: In due season he sent a slave to the cultivators so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. The cultivators, however, sent him away empty-handed, after beating him.

25894.label: Luke 20:11
25894.text: But again he sent another slave. That one also they beat and humiliated and sent away empty-handed.

25895.label: Luke 20:12
25895.text: Yet again he sent a third; this one also they wounded and threw out.

25896.label: Luke 20:13
25896.text: At this the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What should I do? I will send my son, the beloved. They will likely respect this one.’

25897.label: Luke 20:14
25897.text: When the cultivators caught sight of him, they reasoned with one another, saying, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him so that the inheritance may become ours.’

25898.label: Luke 20:15
25898.text: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do to them?

25899.label: Luke 20:16
25899.text: He will come and kill these cultivators and will give the vineyard to others.” On hearing this, they said: “Never may that happen!”

25900.label: Luke 20:17
25900.text: But he looked straight at them and said: “What, then, does this mean where it is written: ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the chief cornerstone’?

25901.label: Luke 20:18
25901.text: Everyone falling on that stone will be shattered. As for anyone on whom it falls, it will crush him.”

25902.label: Luke 20:19
25902.text: The scribes and the chief priests then sought to get their hands on him in that very hour, but they feared the people, for they realized that he told this illustration with them in mind.

25903.label: Luke 20:20
25903.text: And after observing him closely, they sent men whom they had secretly hired to pretend that they were righteous in order to catch him in his speech, so as to turn him over to the government and to the authority of the governor.

25904.label: Luke 20:21
25904.text: And they questioned him, saying: “Teacher, we know you speak and teach correctly and show no partiality, but you teach the way of God in line with truth:

25905.label: Luke 20:22
25905.text: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”

25906.label: Luke 20:23
25906.text: But he detected their cunning and said to them:

25907.label: Luke 20:24
25907.text: “Show me a de·narʹi·us. Whose image and inscription does it have?” They said: “Caesar’s.”

25908.label: Luke 20:25
25908.text: He said to them: “By all means, then, pay back Caesar’s things to Caesar but God’s things to God.”

25909.label: Luke 20:26
25909.text: Well, they were not able to trap him in his speech before the people, but amazed at his answer, they became silent.

25910.label: Luke 20:27
25910.text: However, some of the Sadducees, those who say there is no resurrection, came and asked him:

25911.label: Luke 20:28
25911.text: “Teacher, Moses wrote us, ‘If a man’s brother dies, leaving a wife, but he was childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’

25912.label: Luke 20:29
25912.text: Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife but died childless.

25914.label: Luke 20:31
25914.text: and the third married her. Likewise even all seven; they died and left no children.

25916.label: Luke 20:33
25916.text: Consequently, in the resurrection, whose wife will she become? For the seven had her as a wife.”

25917.label: Luke 20:34
25917.text: Jesus said to them: “The children of this system of things marry and are given in marriage,

25918.label: Luke 20:35
25918.text: but those who have been counted worthy of gaining that system of things and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.

25919.label: Luke 20:36
25919.text: In fact, neither can they die anymore, for they are like the angels, and they are God’s children by being children of the resurrection.

25920.label: Luke 20:37
25920.text: But that the dead are raised up, even Moses made known in the account about the thornbush, when he calls Jehovah ‘the God of Abraham and God of Isaac and God of Jacob.’

25921.label: Luke 20:38
25921.text: He is a God, not of the dead, but of the living, for they are all living to him.”

25922.label: Luke 20:39
25922.text: In response some of the scribes said: “Teacher, you spoke well.”

25923.label: Luke 20:40
25923.text: For they no longer had the courage to ask him a single question.

25924.label: Luke 20:41
25924.text: In turn he asked them: “How is it they say that the Christ is David’s son?

25925.label: Luke 20:42
25925.text: For David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘Jehovah said to my Lord: “Sit at my right hand

25926.label: Luke 20:43
25926.text: until I place your enemies as a stool for your feet.”’

25927.label: Luke 20:44
25927.text: David, therefore, calls him Lord; so how is he his son?”

25928.label: Luke 20:45
25928.text: Then, while all the people were listening, he said to his disciples:

25929.label: Luke 20:46
25929.text: “Beware of the scribes who like to walk around in robes and who love greetings in the marketplaces and front seats in the synagogues and the most prominent places at evening meals,

25930.label: Luke 20:47
25930.text: and who devour the houses of the widows and for show make long prayers. These will receive a more severe judgment.”

25931.label: Luke 21:1
25931.text: Now as he looked up, he saw the rich dropping their gifts into the treasury chests.

25932.label: Luke 21:2
25932.text: Then he saw a needy widow drop in two small coins of very little value,

25933.label: Luke 21:3
25933.text: and he said: “Truly I say to you that this poor widow put in more than they all did.

25934.label: Luke 21:4
25934.text: For all of these put in gifts out of their surplus, but she, out of her want, put in all the means of living she had.”

25935.label: Luke 21:5
25935.text: Later, when some were speaking about the temple, how it was adorned with fine stones and dedicated things,

25936.label: Luke 21:6
25936.text: he said: “As for these things that you now see, the days will come when not a stone will be left upon a stone and not be thrown down.”

25937.label: Luke 21:7
25937.text: Then they questioned him, saying: “Teacher, when will these things actually be, and what will be the sign when these things are to occur?”

25938.label: Luke 21:8
25938.text: He said: “Look out that you are not misled, for many will come on the basis of my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The due time is near.’ Do not go after them.

25939.label: Luke 21:9
25939.text: Furthermore, when you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified. For these things must take place first, but the end will not occur immediately.”

25940.label: Luke 21:10
25940.text: Then he said to them: “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.

25941.label: Luke 21:11
25941.text: There will be great earthquakes, and in one place after another food shortages and pestilences; and there will be fearful sights and from heaven great signs.

25942.label: Luke 21:12
25942.text: “But before all these things happen, people will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to the synagogues and prisons. You will be brought before kings and governors for the sake of my name.

25943.label: Luke 21:13
25943.text: It will result in your giving a witness.

25944.label: Luke 21:14
25944.text: Therefore, resolve in your hearts not to rehearse beforehand how to make your defense,

25945.label: Luke 21:15
25945.text: for I will give you words and wisdom that all your opposers together will not be able to resist or dispute.

25946.label: Luke 21:16
25946.text: Moreover, you will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death,

25947.label: Luke 21:17
25947.text: and you will be hated by all people because of my name.

25948.label: Luke 21:18
25948.text: But not even a hair of your heads will perish.

25949.label: Luke 21:19
25949.text: By your endurance you will preserve your lives.

25950.label: Luke 21:20
25950.text: “However, when you see Jerusalem surrounded by encamped armies, then know that the desolating of her has drawn near.

25951.label: Luke 21:21
25951.text: Then let those in Ju·deʹa begin fleeing to the mountains, let those in the midst of her leave, and let those in the countryside not enter into her,

25952.label: Luke 21:22
25952.text: because these are days for meting out justice in order that all the things written may be fulfilled.

25953.label: Luke 21:23
25953.text: Woe to the pregnant women and those nursing a baby in those days! For there will be great distress on the land and wrath against this people.

25954.label: Luke 21:24
25954.text: And they will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations; and Jerusalem will be trampled on by the nations until the appointed times of the nations are fulfilled.

25955.label: Luke 21:25
25955.text: “Also, there will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth anguish of nations not knowing the way out because of the roaring of the sea and its agitation.

25956.label: Luke 21:26
25956.text: People will become faint out of fear and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

25957.label: Luke 21:27
25957.text: And then they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

25958.label: Luke 21:28
25958.text: But as these things start to occur, stand up straight and lift up your heads, because your deliverance is getting near.”

25959.label: Luke 21:29
25959.text: With that he told them an illustration: “Notice the fig tree and all the other trees.

25960.label: Luke 21:30
25960.text: When they are budding, you see it for yourselves and know that now the summer is near.

25961.label: Luke 21:31
25961.text: Likewise also you, when you see these things happening, know that the Kingdom of God is near.

25962.label: Luke 21:32
25962.text: Truly I say to you that this generation will by no means pass away until all things happen.

25963.label: Luke 21:33
25963.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.

25964.label: Luke 21:34
25964.text: “But pay attention to yourselves that your hearts never become weighed down with overeating and heavy drinking and anxieties of life, and suddenly that day be instantly upon you

25965.label: Luke 21:35
25965.text: as a snare. For it will come upon all those dwelling on the face of the whole earth.

25966.label: Luke 21:36
25966.text: Keep awake, then, all the time making supplication that you may succeed in escaping all these things that must occur and in standing before the Son of man.”

25967.label: Luke 21:37
25967.text: So by day he would be teaching in the temple, but by night he would go out and lodge on the mountain called the Mount of Olives.

25968.label: Luke 21:38
25968.text: And all the people would come to him early in the morning to hear him in the temple.

25969.label: Luke 22:1
25969.text: Now the Festival of the Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was getting near.

25970.label: Luke 22:2
25970.text: And the chief priests and the scribes were looking for an effective way to get rid of him, because they were afraid of the people.

25971.label: Luke 22:3
25971.text: Then Satan entered into Judas, the one called Is·carʹi·ot, who was numbered among the Twelve,

25972.label: Luke 22:4
25972.text: and he went off and talked with the chief priests and temple captains about how to betray him to them.

25973.label: Luke 22:5
25973.text: They were delighted at this and agreed to give him silver money.

25974.label: Luke 22:6
25974.text: So he consented and began looking for a good opportunity to betray him to them without a crowd around.

25975.label: Luke 22:7
25975.text: The day of the Unleavened Bread now arrived, on which the Passover sacrifice must be offered;

25976.label: Luke 22:8
25976.text: so Jesus sent Peter and John, saying: “Go and get the Passover ready for us to eat.”

25977.label: Luke 22:9
25977.text: They said to him: “Where do you want us to get it ready?”

25978.label: Luke 22:10
25978.text: He said to them: “Look! When you enter into the city, a man carrying an earthenware water jar will meet you. Follow him into the house that he enters.

25979.label: Luke 22:11
25979.text: And say to the landlord of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you: “Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’

25980.label: Luke 22:12
25980.text: And that man will show you a large, furnished upper room. Get it ready there.”

25981.label: Luke 22:13
25981.text: So they left and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared for the Passover.

25982.label: Luke 22:14
25982.text: So when the hour came, he reclined at the table along with the apostles.

25983.label: Luke 22:15
25983.text: And he said to them: “I have greatly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer;

25984.label: Luke 22:16
25984.text: for I tell you, I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the Kingdom of God.”

25985.label: Luke 22:17
25985.text: And accepting a cup, he gave thanks and said: “Take this and pass it from one to the other among yourselves,

25986.label: Luke 22:18
25986.text: for I tell you, from now on, I will not drink again from the product of the vine until the Kingdom of God comes.”

25987.label: Luke 22:19
25987.text: Also, he took a loaf, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying: “This means my body, which is to be given in your behalf. Keep doing this in remembrance of me.”

25988.label: Luke 22:20
25988.text: Also, he did the same with the cup after they had the evening meal, saying: “This cup means the new covenant by virtue of my blood, which is to be poured out in your behalf.

25989.label: Luke 22:21
25989.text: “But look! the hand of my betrayer is with me at the table.

25990.label: Luke 22:22
25990.text: For, indeed, the Son of man is going his way according to what has been determined; all the same, woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”

25991.label: Luke 22:23
25991.text: So they began to discuss among themselves which one of them could really be about to do this.

25992.label: Luke 22:24
25992.text: However, there also arose a heated dispute among them over which one of them was considered to be the greatest.

25993.label: Luke 22:25
25993.text: But he said to them: “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those having authority over them are called Benefactors.

25994.label: Luke 22:26
25994.text: You, though, are not to be that way. But let the one who is the greatest among you become as the youngest, and the one taking the lead as the one ministering.

25995.label: Luke 22:27
25995.text: For which one is greater, the one dining or the one serving? Is it not the one dining? But I am among you as the one serving.

25996.label: Luke 22:28
25996.text: “However, you are the ones who have stuck with me in my trials;

25997.label: Luke 22:29
25997.text: and I make a covenant with you, just as my Father has made a covenant with me, for a kingdom,

25998.label: Luke 22:30
25998.text: so that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom, and sit on thrones to judge the 12 tribes of Israel.

25999.label: Luke 22:31
25999.text: “Simon, Simon, look! Satan has demanded to have all of you to sift you as wheat.

26000.label: Luke 22:32
26000.text: But I have made supplication for you that your faith may not give out; and you, once you have returned, strengthen your brothers.”

26001.label: Luke 22:33
26001.text: Then he said to him: “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death.”

26002.label: Luke 22:34
26002.text: But he said: “I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not crow today until you have denied knowing me three times.”

26003.label: Luke 22:35
26003.text: He also said to them: “When I sent you out without a money bag and a food pouch and sandals, you did not lack anything, did you?” They said: “No!”

26004.label: Luke 22:36
26004.text: Then he said to them: “But now let the one who has a money bag take it, likewise a food pouch, and let the one who has no sword sell his outer garment and buy one.

26005.label: Luke 22:37
26005.text: For I tell you that what is written must be accomplished in me, namely, ‘He was counted with lawless ones.’ For this is being fulfilled concerning me.”

26006.label: Luke 22:38
26006.text: Then they said: “Lord, look! here are two swords.” He said to them: “It is enough.”

26007.label: Luke 22:39
26007.text: On leaving, he went as was his custom to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples also followed him.

26008.label: Luke 22:40
26008.text: On arriving at the place, he said to them: “Carry on prayer so that you do not enter into temptation.”

26009.label: Luke 22:41
26009.text: And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw away, and he bent his knees and began to pray,

26010.label: Luke 22:42
26010.text: saying: “Father, if you want to, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, let, not my will, but yours take place.”

26011.label: Luke 22:43
26011.text: Then an angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him.

26012.label: Luke 22:44
26012.text: But he was in such agony that he kept praying more earnestly; and his sweat became as drops of blood falling to the ground.

26013.label: Luke 22:45
26013.text: When he rose from prayer and went to the disciples, he found them slumbering, exhausted from grief.

26014.label: Luke 22:46
26014.text: He said to them: “Why are you sleeping? Get up and keep praying, so that you do not enter into temptation.”

26015.label: Luke 22:47
26015.text: While he was still speaking, look! a crowd, and the man called Judas, one of the Twelve, was leading them, and he approached Jesus to kiss him.

26016.label: Luke 22:48
26016.text: But Jesus said to him: “Judas, are you betraying the Son of man with a kiss?”

26017.label: Luke 22:49
26017.text: When those around him saw what was going to happen, they said: “Lord, should we strike with the sword?”

26018.label: Luke 22:50
26018.text: One of them even struck the slave of the high priest, taking off his right ear.

26019.label: Luke 22:51
26019.text: But in reply Jesus said: “That is enough.” And he touched the ear and healed him.

26020.label: Luke 22:52
26020.text: Jesus then said to the chief priests and captains of the temple and elders who had come there for him: “Did you come out with swords and clubs as against a robber?

26021.label: Luke 22:53
26021.text: While I was with you in the temple day after day, you did not lay your hands on me. But this is your hour and the authority of darkness.”

26022.label: Luke 22:54
26022.text: Then they arrested him and led him off, and they brought him into the house of the high priest; but Peter was following at a distance.

26023.label: Luke 22:55
26023.text: When they lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter was sitting among them.

26024.label: Luke 22:56
