26024.text: But a servant girl, seeing him sitting in the light of the fire, looked closely at him and said: “This man was also with him.”

26025.label: Luke 22:57
26025.text: But he denied it, saying: “I do not know him, woman.”

26026.label: Luke 22:58
26026.text: After a short time another person saw him and said: “You too are one of them.” But Peter said: “Man, I am not.”

26027.label: Luke 22:59
26027.text: And after about an hour had passed, another man began insisting strongly: “Certainly this man was also with him, for he is, in fact, a Gal·i·leʹan!”

26028.label: Luke 22:60
26028.text: But Peter said: “Man, I do not know what you are saying.” And instantly, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.

26029.label: Luke 22:61
26029.text: At this the Lord turned and looked straight at Peter, and Peter recalled the statement of the Lord when he had said to him: “Before a rooster crows today, you will disown me three times.”

26030.label: Luke 22:62
26030.text: And he went outside and wept bitterly.

26031.label: Luke 22:63
26031.text: Now the men who held Jesus in custody began to mock him, hitting him;

26032.label: Luke 22:64
26032.text: and after covering his face, they kept asking: “Prophesy! Who is it that struck you?”

26033.label: Luke 22:65
26033.text: And they said many other blasphemous things against him.

26034.label: Luke 22:66
26034.text: And when it became day, the assembly of elders of the people, both chief priests and scribes, gathered together, and they led him into their Sanʹhe·drin hall and said:

26035.label: Luke 22:67
26035.text: “If you are the Christ, tell us.” But he said to them: “Even if I told you, you would not believe it at all.

26036.label: Luke 22:68
26036.text: Moreover, if I questioned you, you would not answer.

26037.label: Luke 22:69
26037.text: However, from now on the Son of man will be seated at the powerful right hand of God.”

26038.label: Luke 22:70
26038.text: At this they all said: “Are you, therefore, the Son of God?” He said to them: “You yourselves are saying that I am.”

26039.label: Luke 22:71
26039.text: They said: “Why do we need further testimony? For we ourselves have heard it out of his own mouth.”

26040.label: Luke 23:1
26040.text: So the multitude got up, one and all, and led him to Pilate.

26041.label: Luke 23:2
26041.text: Then they began to accuse him, saying: “We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding the paying of taxes to Caesar, and saying he himself is Christ a king.”

26042.label: Luke 23:3
26042.text: Now Pilate asked him the question: “Are you the King of the Jews?” In answer he said: “You yourself are saying it.”

26043.label: Luke 23:4
26043.text: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds: “I find no crime in this man.”

26044.label: Luke 23:5
26044.text: But they insisted, saying: “He stirs up the people by teaching throughout all Ju·deʹa, starting from Galʹi·lee even to here.”

26045.label: Luke 23:6
26045.text: On hearing that, Pilate asked whether the man was a Gal·i·leʹan.

26046.label: Luke 23:7
26046.text: After ascertaining that he was under the jurisdiction of Herod, he sent him on to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem in those days.

26047.label: Luke 23:8
26047.text: When Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced greatly. For a considerable time he had been wanting to see Jesus because he had heard much about him, and he was hoping to see some sign performed by him.

26048.label: Luke 23:9
26048.text: So he began to question him at length, but he gave him no answer.

26049.label: Luke 23:10
26049.text: However, the chief priests and the scribes kept standing up and vehemently accusing him.

26050.label: Luke 23:11
26050.text: Then Herod together with his soldiers treated him with contempt, and he mocked him by clothing him with a splendid garment and then sent him back to Pilate.

26051.label: Luke 23:12
26051.text: Herod and Pilate became friends with each other on that very day, for before that they had been at enmity with each other.

26052.label: Luke 23:13
26052.text: Pilate then called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people

26053.label: Luke 23:14
26053.text: and said to them: “You brought this man to me as one inciting the people to revolt. Now look! I examined him in front of you but found in this man no grounds for the charges you are bringing against him.

26054.label: Luke 23:15
26054.text: In fact, neither did Herod, for he sent him back to us, and look! he has done nothing deserving of death.

26055.label: Luke 23:16
26055.text: I will therefore punish him and release him.”

26057.label: Luke 23:18
26057.text: But the whole crowd shouted out: “Do away with this man, and release Bar·abʹbas to us!”

26058.label: Luke 23:19
26058.text: (This man had been thrown into prison for sedition that had occurred in the city and for murder.)

26059.label: Luke 23:20
26059.text: Again Pilate called out to them, because he wanted to release Jesus.

26060.label: Luke 23:21
26060.text: Then they began to yell, saying: “To the stake with him! To the stake with him!”

26061.label: Luke 23:22
26061.text: The third time he said to them: “Why? What bad thing did this man do? I found in him nothing deserving of death; I will therefore punish him and release him.”

26062.label: Luke 23:23
26062.text: At this they became insistent, demanding with loud voices that he be executed, and their voices prevailed.

26063.label: Luke 23:24
26063.text: So Pilate made the decision that their demand be met.

26064.label: Luke 23:25
26064.text: He released the man whom they were demanding, who had been thrown into prison for sedition and murder, but he surrendered Jesus to their will.

26065.label: Luke 23:26
26065.text: Now as they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cy·reʹne, who was coming from the countryside, and they placed the torture stake on him to carry it behind Jesus.

26066.label: Luke 23:27
26066.text: A large number of people were following him, including women who kept beating themselves in grief and wailing for him.

26067.label: Luke 23:28
26067.text: Jesus turned to the women and said: “Daughters of Jerusalem, stop weeping for me. Weep instead for yourselves and for your children;

26068.label: Luke 23:29
26068.text: for look! days are coming when people will say, ‘Happy are the barren women, the wombs that did not give birth and the breasts that did not nurse!’

26069.label: Luke 23:30
26069.text: Then they will start saying to the mountains, ‘Fall over us!’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us over!’

26070.label: Luke 23:31
26070.text: If they do these things when the tree is moist, what will occur when it is withered?”

26071.label: Luke 23:32
26071.text: Two other men, criminals, were also being led off to be executed with him.

26072.label: Luke 23:33
26072.text: And when they got to the place called Skull, they nailed him to the stake there alongside the criminals, one on his right and one on his left.

26073.label: Luke 23:34
26073.text: But Jesus was saying: “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” Furthermore, they cast lots to distribute his garments.

26074.label: Luke 23:35
26074.text: And the people stood looking on. But the rulers were sneering and saying: “Others he saved; let him save himself if he is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”

26075.label: Luke 23:36
26075.text: Even the soldiers mocked him, coming up and offering him sour wine

26076.label: Luke 23:37
26076.text: and saying: “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.”

26077.label: Luke 23:38
26077.text: There was also an inscription over him: “This is the King of the Jews.”

26078.label: Luke 23:39
26078.text: Then one of the criminals hanging there began to speak abusively to him, saying: “You are the Christ, are you not? Save yourself and us too!”

26079.label: Luke 23:40
26079.text: In response the other rebuked him, saying: “Do you not fear God at all, now that you have received the same judgment?

26080.label: Luke 23:41
26080.text: And we rightly so, for we are getting back what we deserve for the things we did; but this man did nothing wrong.”

26081.label: Luke 23:42
26081.text: Then he said: “Jesus, remember me when you get into your Kingdom.”

26082.label: Luke 23:43
26082.text: And he said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”

26083.label: Luke 23:44
26083.text: Well, by now it was about the sixth hour, and yet a darkness fell over all the land until the ninth hour,

26084.label: Luke 23:45
26084.text: because the sunlight failed; then the curtain of the sanctuary was torn down the middle.

26085.label: Luke 23:46
26085.text: And Jesus called out with a loud voice and said: “Father, into your hands I entrust my spirit.” After he said this, he expired.

26086.label: Luke 23:47
26086.text: Because of seeing what occurred, the army officer began to glorify God, saying: “Truly, this man was righteous.”

26087.label: Luke 23:48
26087.text: And when all the crowds that were gathered together there for this spectacle saw the things that occurred, they returned home, beating their chests.

26088.label: Luke 23:49
26088.text: And all those acquainted with him were standing at a distance. Also, women who had accompanied him from Galʹi·lee were there and saw these things.

26089.label: Luke 23:50
26089.text: And look! there was a man named Joseph, a member of the Council, who was a good and righteous man.

26090.label: Luke 23:51
26090.text: (This man had not voted in support of their scheme and action.) He was from Ar·i·ma·theʹa, a city of the Ju·deʹans, and was waiting for the Kingdom of God.

26091.label: Luke 23:52
26091.text: This man went in before Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

26092.label: Luke 23:53
26092.text: And he took it down and wrapped it up in fine linen, and he laid it in a tomb carved in the rock, where no man had yet lain.

26093.label: Luke 23:54
26093.text: Now it was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was about to begin.

26094.label: Luke 23:55
26094.text: But the women who had come with him from Galʹi·lee followed along and took a look at the tomb and saw how his body was laid,

26095.label: Luke 23:56
26095.text: and they went back to prepare spices and perfumed oils. But, of course, they rested on the Sabbath according to the commandment.

26096.label: Luke 24:1
26096.text: But on the first day of the week, they came very early to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.

26097.label: Luke 24:2
26097.text: But they found the stone rolled away from the tomb,

26098.label: Luke 24:3
26098.text: and when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

26099.label: Luke 24:4
26099.text: While they were perplexed about this, look! two men in shining garments stood by them.

26100.label: Luke 24:5
26100.text: The women became frightened and kept their faces turned toward the ground, so the men said to them: “Why are you looking for the living one among the dead?

26101.label: Luke 24:6
26101.text: He is not here, but has been raised up. Recall how he spoke to you while he was yet in Galʹi·lee,

26102.label: Luke 24:7
26102.text: saying that the Son of man must be handed over to sinful men and be executed on the stake and on the third day rise.”

26104.label: Luke 24:9
26104.text: and they returned from the tomb and reported all these things to the Eleven and to all the rest.

26105.label: Luke 24:10
26105.text: They were Mary Magʹda·lene, Jo·anʹna, and Mary the mother of James. Also, the rest of the women with them were telling these things to the apostles.

26106.label: Luke 24:11
26106.text: However, these sayings seemed like nonsense to them, and they would not believe the women.

26107.label: Luke 24:12
26107.text: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb, and stooping forward, he saw only the linen cloths. So he went off, wondering to himself what had occurred.

26108.label: Luke 24:13
26108.text: But look! on that very day, two of them were traveling to a village named Em·maʹus, about seven miles from Jerusalem,

26109.label: Luke 24:14
26109.text: and they were conversing with each other about all these things that had happened.

26110.label: Luke 24:15
26110.text: Now as they were conversing and discussing these things, Jesus himself approached and began walking with them,

26111.label: Luke 24:16
26111.text: but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.

26112.label: Luke 24:17
26112.text: He said to them: “What are these matters that you are debating between yourselves as you walk along?” And they stood still, looking sad.

26113.label: Luke 24:18
26113.text: In answer the one named Cleʹo·pas said to him: “Are you a stranger dwelling alone in Jerusalem and do not know the things that have occurred there during these days?”

26114.label: Luke 24:19
26114.text: He asked them: “What things?” They said to him: “The things concerning Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ, who proved to be a prophet powerful in deed and word before God and all the people;

26115.label: Luke 24:20
26115.text: and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death, and they nailed him to the stake.

26116.label: Luke 24:21
26116.text: But we were hoping that this man was the one who was going to deliver Israel. Yes, and besides all these things, this is the third day since these things occurred.

26117.label: Luke 24:22
26117.text: Moreover, some women from among us also astonished us, for they went early to the tomb

26118.label: Luke 24:23
26118.text: and when they did not find his body, they came saying that they had also seen a supernatural sight of angels, who said he is alive.

26119.label: Luke 24:24
26119.text: Then some of those who were with us went off to the tomb, and they found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him.”

26120.label: Luke 24:25
26120.text: So he said to them: “O senseless ones and slow of heart to believe all the things the prophets have spoken!

26121.label: Luke 24:26
26121.text: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”

26122.label: Luke 24:27
26122.text: And starting with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted to them things pertaining to himself in all the Scriptures.

26123.label: Luke 24:28
26123.text: Finally they got close to the village to which they were traveling, and he made as if to travel on farther.

26124.label: Luke 24:29
26124.text: But they urged him to remain, saying: “Stay with us, because it is almost evening and the day is nearly over.” With that he went in to stay with them.

26125.label: Luke 24:30
26125.text: And as he was dining with them, he took the bread, blessed it, broke it, and began handing it to them.

26126.label: Luke 24:31
26126.text: At that their eyes were fully opened and they recognized him; but he disappeared from them.

26127.label: Luke 24:32
26127.text: And they said to each other: “Were not our hearts burning within us as he was speaking to us on the road, as he was fully opening up the Scriptures to us?”

26128.label: Luke 24:33
26128.text: And they got up in that very hour and returned to Jerusalem, and they found the Eleven and those assembled together with them,

26129.label: Luke 24:34
26129.text: who said: “For a fact the Lord was raised up, and he appeared to Simon!”

26130.label: Luke 24:35
26130.text: Then they related the events on the road and how he became known to them by the breaking of the bread.

26131.label: Luke 24:36
26131.text: While they were speaking of these things, he himself stood in their midst and said to them: “May you have peace.”

26132.label: Luke 24:37
26132.text: But because they were terrified and frightened, they imagined that they were seeing a spirit.

26133.label: Luke 24:38
26133.text: So he said to them: “Why are you troubled, and why have doubts come up in your hearts?

26134.label: Luke 24:39
26134.text: See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself; touch me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones just as you see that I have.”

26135.label: Luke 24:40
26135.text: And as he said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.

26136.label: Luke 24:41
26136.text: But while they were still not believing for sheer joy and amazement, he said to them: “Do you have something there to eat?”

26137.label: Luke 24:42
26137.text: So they handed him a piece of broiled fish,

26138.label: Luke 24:43
26138.text: and he took it and ate it before their eyes.

26139.label: Luke 24:44
26139.text: He then said to them: “These are my words that I spoke to you while I was yet with you, that all the things written about me in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets and Psalms must be fulfilled.”

26140.label: Luke 24:45
26140.text: Then he opened up their minds fully to grasp the meaning of the Scriptures,

26141.label: Luke 24:46
26141.text: and he said to them, “This is what is written: that the Christ would suffer and rise from among the dead on the third day,

26142.label: Luke 24:47
26142.text: and on the basis of his name, repentance for forgiveness of sins would be preached in all the nations —starting out from Jerusalem.

26143.label: Luke 24:48
26143.text: You are to be witnesses of these things.

26144.label: Luke 24:49
26144.text: And look! I am sending upon you what my Father promised. You, though, stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.”

26145.label: Luke 24:50
26145.text: Then he led them out as far as Bethʹa·ny, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.

26146.label: Luke 24:51
26146.text: As he was blessing them, he was parted from them and taken up to heaven.

26147.label: Luke 24:52
26147.text: And they did obeisance to him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.

26148.label: Luke 24:53
26148.text: And they were continually in the temple, praising God.
